Omega Strikers is one of those rare multiplayer games that immediately communicates its identity within the first few minutes. Developed and published by Odyssey Interactive, the title takes the familiar objective of scoring goals and transforms it into a frantic contest of positioning, teamwork, and controlled chaos. Rather than leaning solely on traditional sports mechanics, it blends arena combat with hero-based abilities to create something that feels equally inspired by MOBAs, party games, and competitive esports. The premise is simple: guide an energy core into the opposing team's goal while preventing your opponents from doing the same. In execution, however, the game offers considerably more depth than its colorful presentation initially suggests.

Every match revolves around three-player teams, with each participant selecting a Striker from a diverse cast of characters. Each Striker brings a unique set of abilities that influence how they contribute on the field. Some excel at defending the goal with shields and area denial skills, while others specialize in aggressive attacks that can knock enemies out of the arena entirely. This variety gives Omega Strikers a strong sense of replayability, as players are encouraged to experiment with different team compositions and playstyles. The role-based structure also adds a strategic element that rewards communication and coordination, making victories feel earned rather than accidental.

One of the game's greatest strengths is its arena design. The maps are more than decorative backdrops; they actively influence how matches unfold. Certain stages introduce moving hazards, shifting terrain, or environmental effects that demand constant adaptation. A strategy that dominates one arena may struggle on another, forcing players to stay flexible. Combined with the title's fast movement system and responsive controls, these dynamic environments create matches that are consistently exciting. It is not uncommon for games to swing dramatically in the final moments, with a well-timed ability or a perfectly angled shot determining the outcome.

Omega Strikers also succeeds in making progression feel meaningful without placing excessive barriers in front of new players. Additional Strikers can be unlocked through gameplay, while customization systems allow users to fine-tune their preferred approach. Cosmetic items and seasonal content provide further incentives for long-term engagement without compromising competitive integrity. The game's cross-platform support deserves particular recognition, allowing players on PC, consoles, and mobile devices to compete together seamlessly. This accessibility helps maintain an active community and reinforces the developers' commitment to making the experience available to as many players as possible.

From a presentation standpoint, Omega Strikers is bursting with personality. Its anime-inspired visual style complements the energetic nature of the gameplay, and the roster is filled with memorable designs that give the world its own distinct identity. Character animations are smooth and expressive, while the soundtrack effectively amplifies the intensity of each match. Despite the visual chaos that can emerge during heated moments, the game generally maintains excellent readability, ensuring that players can track the action without feeling overwhelmed.

The title is not without flaws, however. Its competitive nature creates a steep learning curve, especially for newcomers entering matches against experienced opponents. Understanding positioning, mastering abilities, and developing map awareness can take time, and the lack of a substantial single-player component means the experience depends heavily on multiplayer participation. Additionally, Odyssey Interactive has reduced major content development in recent years, which means players should not expect the same steady stream of updates that characterized the game's earlier life cycle. Even so, the existing content remains substantial enough to justify spending dozens of hours mastering its systems.

Ultimately, Omega Strikers stands as an impressive example of creative multiplayer design. It takes familiar concepts and combines them into a package that feels fresh, energetic, and highly competitive. While its future may be quieter than originally anticipated, the quality of its core gameplay ensures that it remains worth experiencing. For players seeking a multiplayer title that rewards teamwork, adaptability, and mechanical skill, Omega Strikers continues to deliver one of the most distinctive experiences available on Steam.

Early ranks are miserable to play through. There is no in game tutorial or youtube video that will prepare you for the game you're about to play.

Your mental fortitude will be tested. You will likely quit before you get to the good part. 

I am writing this review to tell you, the hopeful new user who is browsing player feedback to see if Omega Strikers is worth your time: It is not. You can leave it at that. You likely do not have what it takes. This is not gatekeeping. This is the harsh truth.

 You will not be playing The Game for a very likely hundred of hours after starting. I have thousands of hours on this game because I Love This Game. I broadcast North American and European competitive events for this Game That I Love. I am close friends with much of the community and each day I am reminded by them why I play this Game That We Love.

Omega Strikers is not worth your time. But. To love something is to not care about logical things, to not care about things that get in the way. Like time. 

Omega Strikers is worth your Love. 

I love the way I feel playing this game - the control of self expression I have playing the game is umatched. The pure satisfaction I feel when I become the conductor of any given play, digitally dancing across the at times frustrating maps the game offers. 

There is not a feeling more compelling than the adrenaline rush I get when it is the final point of a competitive game, every single one of my senses locked into what is going to happen next, what I can do to win, what I have to do to make sure I don't lose, how I can beat the opponent standing between me and the victory screen. 

And nothing compares to the catharsis of pulling off that win. 

Honestly, the feeling of losing is numbed by the fact that for a brief moment I was part of something that connected me so strongly to the 5 other players on the field - because trust me: in those moments of extremely high tension, you can tell just by the way everyone else is playing. They feel exactly the same as you do. For a brief moment in time we were taken somewhere special, a place that only existed for the six of us. And I wouldn't trade that for anything. Not all the time in the world could compare. 

So if you are someone who feels strongly about gaming, especially competitively: 

Omega strikers is not worth your time. Omega strikers is worth your love. Please try it, and if you can manage not to give up, I hope to see you in my games.

Now that Omega Strikers has become my most played game of all time, and the only game I keep up with competitively anymore, I should probably write a review.

Who knew that League of Legends soccer was a great blueprint for a multiplayer game? Well there was Windjammers, but that was exclusively 1v1 as far as I can remember. But yes, Omega Strikers is a really fun game concept with vivid character design, killer OST, and lots of mechanical depth to grind your teeth into. If anything about this game interests you in the slightest, you should jump right in and give it a try. Join the official discord, or any of the competitive/region groups and find people to play with/learn from. The community loves having new players join.

With that being said I do feel the need to mention a few things:

1. This is a team-based competitive game, making it very easy to get angry with other people or have other people get angry at you. It’s a game at the end of the day so just have fun and get better at your own speed.
2. The balancing of this game sometimes feels as if we’re on a tightrope. The meta shifts quite often and some of the previous patches have been, questionable? It’s all subjective and not something you need to think about when just starting out, but as you get deeper into Omega Strikers you will start to really feel it.
3. The best experience you can have with this game is bringing a group of friends into the game or making those friends through Omega Strikers itself. In-houses and scrim matches are very fun and great ways to learn the systems. You just need the 5 other people for it. I was lucky enough to join my friend’s group when starting out but I assume that the more common experience is to try this game out on a whim solo and just feel confused the entire time. I had even quit the game years ago before coming back due to that reason.
4. Yea, solo queue is a hell. Long queue times, and the smaller player base means that it can be difficult for the game to give you an even rank spread within your match. Just don’t be too surprised if you reach Diamond and start somehow playing against Pro League players.
5. You’ll need to rely on community resources, guides, and good old elbow grease to learn this game. Honestly if you’re into fighting games then this isn’t a new concept, but even those games usually have some kind of training mode, tutorials, and combo trials to get you started. Meanwhile Omega Strikers still doesn’t let you test awakenings in practice mode.

With all of that being said, this is still one of my favorite games of all time. I somehow started as a Luna one-trick who couldn’t imagine leaving Gold, and 1500 hours later I’m a Pro League goalie who is trying to place in tournaments. There always felt like something to strive for and I’ve improved so much just by putting in that time towards something I enjoyed. This game has given me so many frustrations and incredible moments and I have never experienced that with any other game I’ve played. I love Omega Strikers and at least for the foreseeable future that will not change. There are so many things I could wish for Odyssey Interactive to have done in order to keep making new content for this game, but this is the game we have now and I’m just happy they bother to keep the servers running, as jank as everything can be.

Which to sum it up leads to some games feeling different even if you only main 1 or 2 champions as the stats and the abilities impact can vary every game depending on what choices you are given and your own strategy in the awakening draft.

It's too bad Odyssey decided to move on to new projects instead of working on this one more. The game has the disappointing system where you either have to buy too many or too little of the irl money only currency for the cosmetics you want. The player base is way too small making it almost impossible to queue at certain times of the day. Game is cooked.

Norms queue is completely compromised by a single player.
There's a player that's both Pro League rank(highest rank achievable) + Tournament player that ONLY duo queues norms with the best of the best regulars in norm.

What this does is that it creates 2 common scenarios, both heavily unfavorable for the opposing team.
1) Two newbies(fresh rookie~gold) get pulled in, one on each team.
2) Opposing team either matches the overall average MMR or is disadvantaged. This is b/c the 3rd brings the MMR down(usually diamond+). Also no one on the opposing team ever matches their peak ranks.

Why is this problematic? Because in scenario one, your 3rd is going to get exploited and is also near impossible to coordinate b/c of the rank gap. The other team doesn't really need the 3rd b/c of the duo synergy and being the highest skilled players in that game. Also the newbies end up getting soft flamed on both sides which results in VERY frequent RQs. Very miserable experience for the newbies, esp if that's their first impression!!

In scenario two, you get duo + synergy gapped. Even if you have higher team MMR average, you simply cannot beat the team synergy. For the record, this guy apparently has a 94%+ WR btw.

Games are unfun when it's rigged against you. They might even be partially responsible for some of the regulars quitting the game b/c the games against them are simply not enjoyable. With a dwindling population, you cannot escape them from norms, both new or regular, b/c match making eventually caves the longer the queue goes. When they're on, you will match with them.

That being said, this post will probably get meme'd + copy pasta'd. I simply dislike bad matchmaking and all of what I've said has been an observed experience as a frequent regular of this game. I'm not obsessed with this individual but I do pick up on patterns after being matched against them over and over and over again. The player population is so small I can recognize all the regulars that play norms except for incognitos(can recognize a few actually).

All that needs to be done is disable duo/tri queue in norms(also covers duo/tri q smurfs). The population is so small you can still play with your friends if you queue together, only this time there's a fighting chance on both teams when match making isn't rigged.

Omega Strikers – A Fast-Paced Footbrawler with Strategic Depth

Omega Strikers is a free-to-play, cross-platform 3v3 footbrawler that combines the fast-paced action of Rocket League with the strategic depth of MOBAs. Developed by Odyssey Interactive, the game offers a unique blend of skill-based gameplay and team coordination.

Gameplay & Mechanics
The core gameplay revolves around knocking a giant puck into the opposing team's goal while utilizing each Striker's unique abilities. Matches are played over three quick rounds, allowing players to adapt and strategize between rounds. The arenas feature dynamic hazards and buffs, adding an extra layer of strategy to each match.

Characters & Customization
With a growing roster of diverse Strikers, each character offers distinct playstyles and abilities. Players can unlock new Strikers through gameplay and customize their appearance with various skins and emotes. The Striker Affinity system rewards players for playing with specific characters, unlocking additional cosmetic items.

Cross-Platform Play & Progression
Omega Strikers supports full cross-play and cross-progression across PC, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, Xbox, and mobile platforms. This ensures that players can compete with friends regardless of their platform and carry their progress across devices.

Community & Longevity
The game has a dedicated and growing community, with frequent updates introducing new content and features. However, some players have expressed concerns about the lack of certain features, such as a practice mode and the ability to view full match history.

Final Verdict
Omega Strikers offers a refreshing take on the competitive multiplayer genre, combining fast-paced action with strategic depth. Its unique gameplay mechanics and cross-platform support make it a standout title in the free-to-play arena.

This is essentially a love letter to Strikers I guess.

The gameplay? Phenomenal.
The music? Phenomenal.
The dev team? Phenomenal.

Omega Strikers is not a perfect game, but by God is it close. There is so much to love, the game absolutely oozes with character, the core gameplay loop is amazing, and even a slight difference in skill between the two teams can swing the momentum entirely.

This is the closest thing I get to playing a "sports" game, and it nails the suspense, thrill, and heartbreak of a real match. Blowouts are crushing. Close games and match points put you at genuine heart attack risk. Friendly shutouts are brutal. The basics of good core control and field positioning are critical for success, the abilities always keep you guessing and add another layer of depth to every interaction, and one good awakening pick can turn the tide of a match. With everything together there's such a high skill ceiling it's almost unreal. You feel it at every level, every rank, every increment. Yet, you can play these close matches all in good fun, or with the utmost amount of sweat humanly possible, just depends on how the teams play.

The art design is fantastic. Characters are all unique and recognizable, the voice acting is A+, and all the abilities/animations flow with their designs and personalities. UI is clean albeit buggy at times, but map design is awesome and sets you in a lively world/environment. The music is top-notch, each character having their own version of the theme and having it play in match for MVP is a beautiful touch. The emotes, somehow, are somehow able to not only perfectly capture the essence of the characters they depict, but the memes they are often inspired by. They don't feel forced, they don't feel... "artificial" even. They have soul. The whole game has soul. And that's hard to find nowadays.

(This extreme skill ceiling can make it extremely difficult for new players to engage with the game however, I have had quite a few friends try it out but lose interest fairly quickly getting their ass kicked 15 matches in a row. The enemy team can always smell blood in the water when they detect a new player and getting heavily bullied in a strikers match is enough to break any man)

I don't blame the devs for the downturn in players. I don't blame them for having to wind-down production on new strikers content either, they were very honest in their video detailing the shift and I totally understand. It's sad that such a good game will likely be further buried as time goes on but me and my friends will continue to play strikers as long as we can find a match.

Thank you Ody Team, and I hope you can find success in future endeavors.

Note- I played this game almost non stop and exclusively on mobile at launch and on-and-off throughout, so my experiences will likely be different. Still sad they discontinued it on mobile, pc is hard for me :(

Zero pay to win, with the only purchases being completely cosmetic aside from absurd prices of premium currency for characters, in a game where every character can be fairly quickly unlocked through the free currency earned by just playing the game, so there isn't an incentive to buy them anyway. Actually skill based gameplay and all characters are relatively balanced. The gameplay in itself is a lot of fun, which of course is a personal opinion, but I don't really find myself enjoying games of similar or the same genre, so that to me, just shows how great it is. This really could have been a perfect game.

Of course, this is coming from someone who has had experience on the game since launch, when the game had many players, and from what I have heard, the new player experience nowadays is a joke, which makes sense. A lackluster tutorial (I don't even remember doing a tutorial when I first played), combined with a low player count likely consisted of veteran players who have been playing since launch, or even before that, and a new player likely wouldn't feel inclined to play again if their first experience doesn't go well.

I personally don't think the game is completely dead. PC for me at least, finding a match usually doesn't take longer than 30 seconds to a minute (mobile could take almost 10 minutes to find one before discontinuation), though due to the low player count, I found myself often matching with people i'd played with in previous matches, which can be a good or bad thing depending on the person. I don't enjoy how the game pretty much became a "Discord game," due to it's lower player count, as I i'd rather not interact with other people much, especially over the internet. (personal problem) Though, this could be a benefit to some, as the game has a very tight knit and active, albeit small community.

Really, I wish this game stayed as popular as it did at launch. It really did change my life for a while because of it's very welcoming and active community, the only community I ever felt comfortable in, and that's saying a lot. I urge anyone who is even remotely interested in it to please, give it a try. Even better if you have somebody you know who is also interested or plays it, as despite it's flaws, both in and out of the game's control, the core game itself will always be amazing.

Omega Strikers is a fast-paced, 3v3 knockout brawler that blends air hockey with MOBA-style abilities. It’s easy to pick up, hard to master, and full of chaotic moments. But does it have enough depth to keep players hooked?

The Good:
✅ Unique & Fast-Paced Gameplay: A mix of air hockey, fighting, and strategy.
✅ Diverse Character Roster: Each striker has distinct abilities and playstyles.
✅ Skill-Based, Not Pay-to-Win: Victory depends on mechanics and teamwork, not microtransactions.
✅ Perfect for Quick Matches: Fast games make it ideal for casual or competitive play.

The Bad:
❌ Matchmaking Can Be Inconsistent: Team balance isn't always great.
❌ Limited Game Modes: Could use more variety to stay fresh long-term.
❌ Steep Learning Curve: Some characters feel harder to master than others.
❌ Community & Player Base Growth?: Will it sustain a strong player base over time?

Final 
If you love fast-paced, competitive games with unique mechanics, Omega Strikers is worth playing. It’s fun, challenging, and rewarding, but its long-term appeal will depend on new content and a growing community.

Booting up the game to a mediocre tutorial that tells you what your buttons do, into an experience of an extreme grind for new characters to play is pretty awful. This also doesn't mention the hell that is rookie - bronze for new players. When skilled players make new alts for the game and get them up to rank, this means they absolutely stomp those lower players and it sucks because then they don't learn on either side and keep ping ponging the ball at each other till somebody scores. This is not fun.
However, if you can get past the new player experience the game becomes a whole lot more fun and is enhanced by joining discords the game is linked to. I just think that if Ody came back to do a little bit more work than they usually do since the stop of major content updates, they could overhall the new player experience and maybe keep some players engaged with the game (which is why they stopped major content updates in the first place).

My opinions for fixes could include:
-Making characters cheaper/have a weekly free rotation. 
        Not being able to play the characters in a real setting other than the practice range before your 30 to 60 game grind means people will buy their character and hate them, then uninstall because they don't want to go another 30 to 60 games for another character.
-Have a little bit more detail in the tutorial for making plays other than hitting the ball forward.
        Its been a while since I did it last (I know there were some updates) but I just think the newer players need a bit more help than you would realize.
-Give more lp for hotstreaks in lower elos. 
        This will get those more experienced players up to their skill level quicker while leaving the low level areas for the new players to become more comfortable with the game.
-Add more emphasis on learning character abilities.
        Characters like rune (my beloved), luna, nao will frustrate newer players because their abilities aren't directly linked to their character (IE pillar, nuke, secondary mine) so newer players will be confused and wonder what just scored on them. Maybe update the ability screen to show video footage of the ability being used, as text isn't good enough.

Anyways now that I have randomly ranted after booting up marvel rivals, please take some of this in mind if you are a new player (or a dev tryna fix stuff).

An Identity Crisis in the Arena

Omega Strikers had real potential. On paper, it's a fast-paced 3v3 blend of air hockey, MOBAs, and anime flair—a fresh take in a sea of uninspired free-to-play titles. But while the game bursts with style, its execution leaves much to be desired.

Gameplay: Fast, Flashy… and Frustrating
Matches are chaotic in all the wrong ways. While the core concept of knocking a core (ball) into a goal seems simple, the game often devolves into button mashing and positional confusion. Character abilities are flashy, but they lack clarity—making it hard to track who’s doing what, especially in close quarters. You often die or lose a goal without understanding how or why it happened.

The skill ceiling is high, which would be great—except it feels like the learning curve is artificially steep. There's a massive gulf between casual and sweaty ranked play, and with poor matchmaking, new players are either carried or crushed. Neither is fun.

Characters: Style Over Substance
There’s a solid roster of quirky, anime-inspired strikers—but balance is all over the place. Some characters (like Juliette) feel overpowered in every role, while others (like Atlas or Drek’ar) often feel clunky, underwhelming, or just… boring. Buffs and nerfs are frequent but inconsistent, leading to constant shifts in viability with no real sense of meta stability.

Also, it’s hard to care about the characters. The game throws lore and personality at you without giving you reasons to be invested. Voice lines repeat constantly, and after the tenth "Let’s gooooo!" it starts to grate.

Monetization & Progression
The free-to-play model isn’t egregious, but it’s not great either. Unlocking characters feels grindy, and cosmetic items are overpriced for how generic most of them look. Worse, the seasonal reward system feels like it was designed to trick you into logging in rather than reward meaningful engagement.

Technical & UI Issues
Menus are cluttered and slow. Queue times can be weirdly long for a game that claims to be competitive and accessible. The controls—especially on Switch and mobile—are clunky, and it feels like the game wasn’t designed with these platforms in mind. Desyncs and lag spikes also still occur far more often than they should.

Final Verdict
Omega Strikers looks like a blast and plays like a mess. Beneath its energetic exterior is a game struggling to figure out what it wants to be—esports-ready? Party-friendly? Skill-based? RNG-laced? Until it finds its footing, it remains a stylish but forgettable brawler in a crowded market.

Skip this unless you’re willing to put up with jank, imbalance, and a game still searching for its soul.

Omega Strikers is the first (currently only) competitive sports game I've enjoyed
While it has flaws, which I will mention. The pros far outweigh the cons for me
TLDR Sports with PvP done right

Pros:
- Fast paced action (especially once you scale and/or when overtime hits. I generally don't enjoy slow games)
- Freedom (You can play any role with any character, even if you locked in a different role. Goalie died? Play goalie yourself)
- Devs (They take feedback seriously, balancing better than most. Also you can see them in queue, they play their own game)
- Fully free to play (The only $ would be non-game impacting cosmetics)
- Fun (Skills are fun to use, core is fun to hit, great character design, just overall enjoyable)

Cons: 
It's a shame many fixes came slow after launch, by the time people already quit the game so the playerbase is small
 I only have 2 current concerns

- Matchmaking - This has plagued the game since release. Over 2 years later it's improved, but as a Pro League I should not be matched up with/vs Platinums in ranked at all. This ruins the game for everyone
Rank context (with 3 divisions in each): Platinum > Diamond > Challenger > Omega > Pro League

- Server/Lag - If you live far East/West or Canada then you will have to deal with high ping occasionally. This has improved after release due to central servers (Texas and Colorado), and while I am not certain what could be done to fix it fully

Again, the pros outweigh the cons for me

Game bugged out threw me into comp for my first player match despite me literally not having it unlocked because I was still working on the quests to unlock it. (Which was merely a part of the beginner progress quests, when I had absolutely no desire to play comp) Did not help that my only matches up to that point were bot matches where I was trying to get my footing with the game. Subsequent normal matches all had players who would just absolutely clown on me and be very rude the entire time regardless of what character or role I tried to play.

Really tried to give this one a shot, but even playing bot matches and trying out all the characters I had available to me, most of the kits just felt really clunky and in need of some more polish. I think there was only one character that seemed friendly to newer players out of everyone I tried. (Shoutouts to Dubu)  Positioning seems super important in this game, and unfortunately all the characters are so punishingly slow that even if you recognize that you need to move you won't be getting to your destination any time soon with the sluggish move speed. Even with characters that have speed buffs that held overwhelmingly true with everyone I played.

I ended up writing down a list that would summarize each of the character's kits for me and let me narrow down who I did and didn't like so that I could more easily decide who to try next, because the time to pick characters goes by a little bit too fast. You can say that for every single menu that requires you to read and make decisions. I'm sure it's fine for veterans of the game, but it makes it abysmally hard to learn what I'm doing. Not to mention unlike other hero-based games there's not really any time to breathe and try to understand your abilities more. Practice mode and bot matches were practically a necessity for me to even simply get my bearings, especially since the game lacks a lot of visual feedback that may help you understand what's going on at a glance.

Really wanted to give this one a shot, I enjoyed the short matches, but the lengthy matchmaking times leading into the people I played up against being so rude really killed my desire to continue giving this game a chance. I might try to stick it out and see if things improve, but for right now I wouldn't recommend it.

Additional note:
I will say my time in the discord started out very friendly and welcoming, and I was pleased to find a lot of friendly individuals... who then slowly as the day went on got completely flooded out by some just downright toxic individuals flaming each other and being generally hostile to any further questions I had. There are some diamonds in the rough, but good grief did that absolutely sour my desire to keep going. Especially since the toxicity of the discord seemed to correlate directly with how toxic the matchmaking was at that time of day.

The map designs are pretty good, there are some nasty angles you can hit using the layouts. The one downside is that the newer maps feel unnecessarily cluttered.

The matches average about 7 or 8 minutes, so you don't need to worry about being stuck in a match for too long.

I'd recommend giving the game a try. It isn't dead yet, and the devs ARE still maintaining it, so there's no fear that the servers will go down anytime soon. Who knows - Maybe if the player base increases, they'll come back to it.

This is such a great game! It has absolutely amazing graphics, character design, and sound track and is genuinely the most fun game I've played in months. It's complete free to play and the only micro transactions are for cosmetics. The game itself is like team based air hockey with abilities. It has a high skill ceiling and once you get the hang of the game you just get into the flow zone. You start to develop strategy instead of just mindlessly hitting the core (puck) as you realize you can dribble, pass, self pass, fake out, stun enemies and hit the core simultaneously, predict your enemies and pre-fire an ability, find sneaky ways to kill opponents from across the map, etc.

And now for one of my favorite mechanics in this game: Awakenings. Awakenings are buffs/power ups that you can choose in between rounds. It works like a draft where players take turns picking their awakenings and taking it out of the pool for everyone else. Because of this system each game feels completely different. You can build your character in so many different ways and a lot of the perks synergize so well with each other. Whether you want to focus on KOs, long ranged projectiles, teleporting halfway across the map, or becoming twice as big as everyone else there is something for you.

It's a bit hard to get into for beginners as the tutorial is a bit lacking so if you're thinking about picking this game up I'd watch a few of the "tips and tricks for omega strikers" videos on youtube and read through their glossary that they have hidden away (it's the button of a book in the main menu). The tutorial doesn't really explain awakenings, ability tags, and strategy so try and figure that stuff out yourself. 

Another thing that I have to mention is the low player base. The peak players on steam is usually about 500 and because of that queue times can suffer a bit. However depending on the server and time sometimes you won't even notice. I'm in NA servers and when I play between 6pm-11pm Central Time I'll normally join into a game in less than 2 minutes. I hope you guys try this game out! It's free so you might as well give it a shot!

I love this game. I'm a ride or die Omega Strikers player. Great characters on a incredibly solid foundation of gameplay with enough simplicity to get into and enough complexity to leave you always learning and improving and feeling like you have an impact on the game. The skill ceiling is so high but you can do insane plays at all levels of play. There are some problems with some UI (particularly for labbing nerds) but the game looks and sounds fantastic otherwise. The game balance, well, there have been ups and downs with various patches but for 95% of games that occur, the game is winnable as long as you simply play better. Truly unwinnable games don't really happen (or you can tell happen) until you start knocking on the door of high elo.
This leads into the only thing I truly dislike about the game: lack of players. And that isn't just a "I wish more people played this game!" but a legitimate problem the game faces. If there's anything that Omega Strikers Players complain about, it's bad matchmaking. And indeed, *sometimes* it's just the system being bad and making unbalanced teams. But a disturbing amount of the time it's because there isn't enough players to make full games of same ranks, and so the game will have to kidnap lower or higher ranked players for both teams. Even if they're balanced on paper, depending on how the ranks sift out between the goalie or forward positions, the games will be lopsided. This is a problem that unfortunately can only be truly solved by playerbase numbers. No matter how much Ody tweaks MM, there's only so much they can do before queues become untenable just waiting for like an hour for 1 for perfectly balanced MM which would kill the already small playerbase. Ody's already done a lot of tweaking to MM and honestly it's something I, and many other players, have just kinda learned to live with unfortunately. The skeleton crew is already more crew than skeleton as far as I can tell, which I deeply appreciate, so I'm not gonna complain about what they're devoting their maintenance to at this stage of the game.
So if you're getting this game, you should be aware of this. New players actively help remedy what is, in my opinion, Omega Strikers' biggest problem! But also be aware that for the same reason, that playing with your friends to minimize MM problems (at least until you're acclimatized to the game and comfortable to jump into the depths of solo q hell xdd) is probably recommended, unless you're just built different and can handle whatever is thrown at you, bad teammates or strong opponents. The community is pretty decent, unless you join the discord to flame, which you will get clowned for. :JunoClown:

Finally amassing a good 500 hours, I believe I have enough experience to make a thorough review of the game.

[i]Omega Strikers[/i] is a footbrawl, featuring what's essentially a football (soccer) match between strikers (Equivalent to Dota's Heroes as are champions are to League) who hail from a roster of 21 characters as of December 2023. The game features fast paced action where characters must score against the enemy in typical football fashion, with the exception of brawling; each characters some equipped with 3 unique abilities that are a primary, secondary, and an ultimate. Already you can see the MOBA influences! However, there isn't an official roster of classes which let you know from the get-go of who does what (e.g. Support, tank, etc). That information can be gained from the character's in-game information (Yes, you have to read). If I am not mistaken, the tutorial session covers it.

The game modes featured are the following: Competitive, Normal, Quickplay, Custom, Co-op vs AI and Practice. Competitive is just like Normal but with ranks added to them. In both modes, a team is to play against another, scoring 3 goals per set, with 3 sets being the official win condition. Between each set, strikers can get passive buffs from a select screen. However, the order of which the players select depends on the amount of XP given, with the leading MVP of the set having first picks. Quickplay is the same, but instead of 3 sets, you have 1 set of 5 goals to get to win. Custom is self explanatory. Co-op vs AI is when players are put up against bots (and the bots are kinda bad ngl) which serves well to test out characters and for new players to get familiar with some mechanics. Practice is just a solo game where you can familiarize yourself with the strikers, etc. Most people will find themselves within playstyles such as goalie, forward (people who try to get the goals), midfielder (who stay in the mid field and support both forward and goalie if need be), and flex (those who play any roles). Only goalie, forward, and flex are recognized at this time by game. Midfielder is just a convention I see the community makes for their own styles. You can select these roles before queuing for a game to get a match for that style of play.

Since the game is free-to-play, the main revenue comes from the in-game skins. I can't comment on these because I spent like zero dollars on it, haha. Another source of in-come are the emotes, which I never spent money on. Some emotes are free by the way, with special ones being unlocked by codes. Why emotes, though? Odyssey Interactive learned from the MOBA communities that freedom in communication leads to utmost abhorrent display of toxicity! So instead of getting a teammate yelling racial slurs in Spanish or Russian, now you can get them to spam emotes, cute ones too! (Please note, this doesn't stop players to find other ways to express their toxicity.) Mind you, since it is a 3v3, communication is necessary. Sure you have a limited option of choices given such as "Let me defend!" which is often used in exasperation, To avoid scenarios such as when two allies using their abilities at the same time leading to a fumbled shot, voice communication is highly recommended. This is why the Discord exists, to facilitate conversation! The community is nice too, so that's a plus!

I will now condense what I like and dislike about the game in a list.
The Pros:
- The music in this game is a banger. 

- Fast paced action for my neurons, big dopamine rush when "outsmart" (get lucky) the opponents with trickshots and win strike wars.
- Cute emojis (SADBOIS user)

- Fun with friends (this one's important)

- This one is not on the game itself, but the community is pretty nice if you ignore the raging players. Also, toxic players don't seem to like being in the Discord , so that's a plus! (I will find out where the live another way).

- If you feel uncomfortable with your name being shown, you can hide it from other players! (So conveniently nice!)

- Cool characters! (I only played the female characters)

- Trigger did an animation for it.

The cons:
-  You're playing with others: If you have no friends who play this game, solo queuing is a way to go, but be prepared to have a mixed bag of skill and IQ. (New players skip the tutorial and hop into a ranked game for some reason)

- Matchmaking ranks: Even when I was in a platinum bracket, I got with teammates who were silver, bronze or rookies. This led to my derank as well -40 points lost (Yippee!).

- It's fast-paced as in the game can turn into ping-pong on steroids (as it should) making it hard for players to keep up.


Conclusion:
I like the game. Don't like playing with others despite me solo queuing because the community is so nice that I momentarily forget. So nice of them. I'd highly recommend if you're into

Let me tell you, if there were 100 alternate realities, I think I would love this game in every one of them. So my opinion is probably biased but I'll try to write a good review.

First of all, the gameplay is fire. Fast paced but still visually readable, most games will usually have this super hype, dopamine inducing moment that keeps you hooked. Games are pretty quick, ranging from 10 to 20 minutes. The character diversity is pretty good and I do think everyone can find their type of playstyle in one of them. But as a small warning, this game is past it's short golden age. Pretty much, the developpers had to stop developping new maps and characters, not out of lazyness, but because the game was slowly dying. They are now focusing on new projects, but still release patches and rotations. The result is that some have stopped playing, and that the community consists mostly of people that play regularly, which can in fact make the beginner experience quite though. I recommend that if you start out, you join the discord, or one of the smaller community discords in order to be more included and have some tips, the people there are cool!

As you can see in the previews, the game traces inspiration in anime. The characters mostly follow a specific trope done well, but if that is something that could make or break your enjoyment, then you probably won't like it too much (I still encourage trying the game). But if you like the stylised graphics and fun characters... well let's say you didn't see the best part, or should I say hear it. The game's OST is an absolute BANGER. Thank our lord James Landino for giving each character their MVP music. If you perform well enough, you can listen to your character's theme while beating up the other team, which really adds to the feel of the game, trust me.

I recommend to play this game with a friend group, as it makes the fun moments even more hilarious, and the cool ones even cooler.

Omega Strikers – A Competitive Arena Game That Missed the Goal 🚫⚽
🌆 Overview

Omega Strikers is a game that looked like it had everything needed to become the next big competitive multiplayer hit.

Fast matches.

Stylish characters.

A unique combination of air hockey, soccer, and fighting game mechanics.

A colorful anime-inspired world.

On paper, it was an exciting idea.

Unfortunately, the execution never reached the potential it promised.

While the core concept is genuinely creative, Omega Strikers struggles with balancing issues, repetitive gameplay, frustrating matchmaking, and a lack of long-term motivation. What starts as a fresh and exciting experience quickly becomes a grind where the flaws become impossible to ignore.

Instead of becoming the next great competitive arena game, Omega Strikers feels like a missed opportunity.

⚙️ Gameplay & Mechanics
⚽ A Great Idea With Frustrating Execution

The foundation of Omega Strikers is actually brilliant.

Two teams battle in a fast-paced 3v3 arena where the goal is simple:

Hit the core into the opponent's goal.

But underneath that simplicity are layers of strategy.

Players must position themselves, control space, interrupt opponents, manage abilities, and coordinate with teammates.

The problem is that the gameplay often feels less like a test of skill and more like a test of patience.

Matches can quickly become chaotic, with abilities flying everywhere and players getting knocked around constantly. Instead of rewarding smart positioning, many encounters turn into overwhelming ability spam.

The game wants to be competitive, but it often struggles to maintain the precision needed for a true competitive experience.

🎯 Combat & Character Design
✨ Interesting Characters, Uneven Balance

Omega Strikers' biggest strength is its roster.

Every character has a unique personality, visual style, and playstyle.

Some are aggressive attackers.

Some focus on defense.

Others specialize in controlling the battlefield.

The variety creates exciting possibilities and encourages experimentation.

However, balance problems hold the roster back.

Certain characters feel significantly stronger than others, making matches frustrating when facing the same dominant picks repeatedly.

Instead of feeling like every player has equal opportunity, some games feel decided before the match even begins.

A competitive game needs variety.

Omega Strikers often feels like it has favorites.

🏟️ Maps & Match Design
⚠️ Fun Concepts That Become Repetitive

The arenas look great and have creative mechanics that change how matches play.

Different maps introduce obstacles, hazards, and unique layouts that force players to adapt.

But after enough matches, the variety starts to disappear.

The objectives remain identical.

The strategies become predictable.

The same situations happen repeatedly.

A competitive game needs constant reasons to return, and Omega Strikers struggles to provide that feeling.

The first few hours are exciting.

The next several dozen can feel like the same match played over and over.

🎨 Visuals & Presentation
🌈 The Best Part of the Experience

Omega Strikers is undeniably stylish.

The character designs are colorful.

Animations are smooth.

The arenas have personality.

The art direction feels inspired by anime, esports, and arcade games all at once.

Each striker has memorable designs and expressive animations that make the game immediately recognizable.

Unfortunately, great presentation cannot completely hide the gameplay issues underneath.

A beautiful game still needs a reason to keep playing.

🔊 Soundtrack & Atmosphere

The soundtrack matches the energetic style of the game.

The music is upbeat, dramatic, and fits the fast-paced matches.

Sound effects make hits feel impactful, and character abilities have satisfying feedback.

The overall presentation creates the feeling of a major competitive event.

The problem is that the excitement fades when the gameplay starts showing its weaknesses.

🌐 Multiplayer & Replayability
❌ Where Omega Strikers Falls Apart

Competitive multiplayer games survive because players always feel like there is something to chase.

A higher rank.

Better teamwork.

New strategies.

A rewarding progression system.

Omega Strikers struggles here.

Matchmaking can feel inconsistent.

Solo players can become frustrated when team coordination matters so heavily.

Progression often lacks the excitement needed to keep players invested.

The game has the foundation of a great esport, but it never fully builds the structure required to support one.

⚖️ Strengths
✅ What It Does Well
Unique combination of soccer, fighting games, and air hockey mechanics.
Great character designs.
Stylish visuals and animations.
Fast matches that are easy to understand.
Fun moments when teamwork clicks.
Creative arena concepts.
⚠️ Major Weaknesses
Balance issues between characters.
Matches can become chaotic instead of strategic.
Repetitive gameplay loop.
Frustrating solo queue experience.
Limited long-term motivation.
Competitive systems never reach their full potential.
Feels like a game with a great idea that needed more refinement.
💭 Why It Doesn't Work

Omega Strikers proves that having a unique idea is only the beginning.

The concept is excellent.

The presentation is impressive.

The characters are memorable.

But competitive games live and die by their depth, balance, and ability to keep players coming back.

Omega Strikers creates exciting moments, but they are surrounded by too many frustrations.

Instead of feeling like a polished competitive masterpiece, it feels like an unfinished version of what could have been something special.

🏁 Verdict

Omega Strikers is one of those games where you can clearly see the potential.

There is a fantastic idea buried underneath the problems.

The fast-paced gameplay, stylish characters, and creative mechanics show that the developers had a strong vision.

But inconsistent balance, repetitive matches, and a lack of lasting engagement prevent it from reaching greatness.

It is fun in short bursts, but it struggles to become a game players can dedicate hundreds of hours to.

⭐ Final Score: 5.5 / 10 — "A Great Idea That Missed the Shot"

Pros: Creative gameplay concept, excellent art style, fun characters, fast matches, satisfying moments

Cons: Balance problems, repetitive gameplay, weak long-term progression, frustrating matchmaking, wasted potential

Verdict:

"Omega Strikers had the ingredients to become a competitive multiplayer classic, but the final product never fully comes together. It looks incredible, plays well at times, and offers a unique experience—but too many flaws keep it from scoring the winning goal."

The best way to describe Omega Strikers, is League of Legends and Rocket League had a baby. It is a 3v3 “footbrawler” where you play as different Strikers, each with their very own ability. For example, you have Estelle, the ice-wielding, ranged attacker, who shoots out volleys of crystals to hit the ball, very good for covering a large area if you are unsure of hitting the ball. 

Each character has abilities especially dedicated to their role, Estelle’s role for example, is recommended to be forward. There are also goalkeepers, and a few support if that is your thing! The abilities within the game vary quite a lot, so it is very easy to switch up your character and try out a whole new gameplay style. Another great example is X, who is essentially more of a brawler. His gameplay is more around knocking out the enemy team, they can’t hit the ball if they’re dead! And in the wise words of our boy, “X GONNA GIVE IT TO YA!” As you can see, the voice lines in this game get a 5 star alone. 

I must add, since our boy X was brought up - yes, you can straight up murder your opponents. Everyone has a health bar, and hitting them with your abilities does damage. The amount done varies per ability, but you definitely shouldn’t go out of your way for kills unless your character specialises in it. Do not fret though, if you are the target of an X - you can respawn and hope his eyes are on another target!

Every hit on the ball not only influences the direction it takes, but also the speed. Think of Lethal League, where you can supercharge the ball. Yeah, that’s pretty much what you get here, just slow enough that you can actually keep track! You definitely have much more control over the ball than you may think at first, and when you learn the core gameplay, it gets very fun and exciting. If teams are even or 0-0, then overtime will happen until a winner is declared. 

Characters DO have to be unlocked, but you can earn a lot of currency by just playing. You also start with some great free characters! Overall, this game feels like a very fun, and fast-paced competitive game. Bring your friends along and I assure you will be deafening each other.

I have a bit more than a 100 hrs in this game at the time of writing this.
And let me tell you...

YES, this is a good game.
YES, the devs said they put this game on life support while they are developping a new game.
YES, the average skill of the player base is pretty high.
YES, the player base is not that huge (you can still very quickly find a game in lower ranks).
YES, the community is overall pretty nice and kind (check out the official discord server).
But YES, is this game satisfying to git gud at.

Now for some more formal and serious review :

GAMEPLAY :
The game plays good ! This is (way) more than just "League of Legends meets football"... It was meant to be competitive. It is overall quite fast and each map has its own gimmick that players can exploit.
Because abilities can hit the core (the ball), which can bounce off of walls, this game is all about prediction, and reading your opponent's next move to mess with them (kind like a traditionnal fighting game).
The awakening system (item system) allows you to customize and enhance your strkier during the course of the match (more range, increased size, better AoE damage...) and is pretty fun to mess and experiment with.
Another neat mechanic is "stagger" (simmilar to health). Here, you don't die when your stagger reaches 0, but rather when you're ejected off of the field. Each abillity deals some form of knockback, which is greatly increased when your stagger is low.
Sadly there is only a quick tutorial to teach you how to play, which means you'll need to learn about the more intricate mechanics by playing against other players...
Finally, the game has some quite good netcode ! I have the chance of playing with about 50 ms and almost never had a moment where the game felt irresponsive.

CHARACTERS (STRIKERS):
There is quite a variety of characters to choose from and overall they all feel unique in gameplay and design.
Each striker has its own "BS" mechanic whether it is getting invisible, getting big and buffed, covering half the field with an ultra damaging AoE... And the awakening system allows you to play them however you see fit.
Every character has some lore and connexions with one another on top of belonging to a fictional team which makes them very likable. Plus they all have a special theme that plays when you're MVP of a game (these songs are REALLY good by the way!)
(And if you're wondering; YES there are some characters with... "interesting" design...)

CONTENT :
In my opinion, there is not a lot of content to grind for... Once you've unlocked all the strikers and their corresponding taunts (which can take less than 100 hrs if you play more optimally than me) the only thing you can grind is "Striker affinity" which gives you some emotes, titles and more as you play a certain character.
There is a battle pass, but most of the time you'll eventually get what you want if you play regularly.

OTHER/MISCELLANIOUS:
There are 3 main game modes : 
--> Quick play, which gives everyone the same set of 3-4 awakenings and the first team to 5 goals wins.
--> Normal game, where you choose your striker and a strating awakening amongst 2 and play a first to 3 rounds. A round is won by the first team who scores 3 goals. In between rounds, an awakening draft is taking place where the better players choose first.
-->Ranked, which is exactly like a normal game except there is a ban phase before picking your striker.

There is also a server browser if you want to search for some games with a specific type players.
The update cycle is slower than before because the devs are currently focusing on their next game, but we still get once a month some balance changes, bugfixes, quality of life features (but no more events and strikers), skins (once everyone has one they may stop)...
This game is way more enjoyable when playing with others in a voice chat !

Moba + air hockey = happy brain chemicals

[h3] Overview [/h3]
On the surface, this game seems very simple. It's 3v3 air hockey where you run around on the board, and you have abilities to help you hit the puck. 1 goalie, 2 forwards. The ranked mode has a drafting mechanic where you select passive buffs that apply for the rest of the match, and this happens after every round.

There are FAR fewer characters than Dota/LoL, so it doesn't feel too daunting to learn each character's basic playstyle. All characters are unlockable with free currency that is easily obtainable. Zero pay-to-win.

You can't type or voice chat to your team or enemy players, but you CAN select 5 emotes from a large pool to express your feelings. The emotes are very fun and varied. I tilt far less than I would in a Dota match for sure.

[h3] Skill-based gaming [/h3]
This game doesn't have a crazy amount of mechanics, but the skill ceiling is REALLY high. I've played over 150 hours, and my best rank is mid-platinum (above which is high plat, low/mid/high diamond, low/mid?/high challenger). I'm still actively learning and improving (solo AND in a 3-person premade).

Ranked is 100% the best way to approach this game, as there are very few leavers, and the drafting mechanics allow you to come back and win. The number of games that have gone 2/2/2 and come down to the final point...oof.

There are normal/quick play options, but people tend to abandon those, so I'd just use them for warmups and then queue ranked.

[h3] Development and such [/h3]
No more content is planned for this game right now, but it is complete and still receiving balance patches. It's not dead (despite what whiners want to say), although queue times can reach a couple minutes. I'd say a full-length ranked match could achieve 30 minutes, but some are faster. It's in an odd state where we frequently get to rematch people we just played because we both re-queued immediately - which is pretty fun IMO.

[h3] Summary [/h3]
Did this review make sense? I have no idea. This game is super duper fun, has tons of things to practice, and people can't abuse you verbally. I'm really enjoying it, and you're not going to get this quality from many other free games. Opportunity for hype moments is real.

I feel most competitive based games don't feel fun after a while, but Omega Strikers manages to just stay simple, and even if a game does end up in an infuriating loss, the games are like at max 20 minutes. It really is such a fun and refreshing experience no matter what gamemode you're playing. Along with all of this, the art style is this really sick mix between anime and western style looking characters, which gives it it's own unique feel, the soundtrack is pretty good especially for a game that could've just gone without one, and the devs are really cool. My friends and I played this at the end of 2022, yet here I am finally writing about the experience. Omega Strikers was a 3v3 online pvp game, with the players playing a fusion of soccer and hockey. Each player controlled one of the dozen or so characters, with play occurring on a rectangular field. Each team had one goalie, while the other two players positioned themselves as offense and defense. Despite these official positions, none of the players were confined to any specific location. They could roam the field at will. The players kicked the puck which glided like it was on ice. Each Striker kicked with the right click, but also had two regular abilities and an ultimate ability. These abilities included ranged attacks, stronger attacks, multiple attacks at once, or stranger abilities like invisibility, creating a barrier, or healing an ally.

Viewed from an isometric perspective, players tried to put the puck in the opposing team's net, while defending their own. The two main distinguishing features of Omega Strikers was a modular map and the ability to fight. The map, while always rectangular, had barriers placed in the middle and edges. In late 2022 there were six different configurations, determined randomly. One arraignment had a diamond shaped barrier in the middle, while another contained four squares, one in each corner of the field. In combat, the players, in addition to striking the puck, could hit strikers, but only with abilities. Taking too much damage in too short a time staggered the striker. Staggered strikers could be punched off the map. After a short delay they respawned on the pitch, but meanwhile the opposing team played with a one person advantage.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Review: Omega Strikers is a fun MOBA version of air hockey that has an easy entry, but a surprisingly high possible skill ceiling. The community is a lot of fun to interact with (especially compared to good ol' League and Dota) and playing with friends makes for an incredibly addicting and fun experience...assuming you can deal with multiple L's in a row you'll likely get in Casual matches/some Ranked matches and roll with the punches. The gameplay and core concept is simple, but are made unique and fresh with the mechanics/skills available to make a one-of-a-kind gameplay loop like no other in it's class. 

Easy to pick up, unfortunately- also easy to put down, considering the type of gamemode is not for the faint of heart. League of Legends and other MOBAs have the feature of having downtime like farming in lane/walking back/etc. but in Omega Strikers there is always action happening- you only stop when you are respawning...which sounds like a good thing, but giving 100% 100% of the time can be pretty stressful, especially in games where the score is 2-3 (8-9 goals scored, around 18+ minutes of constant stress)...damn is it fun, though. 

If you want a game that really makes you feel every second, every hit, every specific change in position matters- this game is for you! It rewards players for being a good teammate and making reads, causing 18 minute games to feel like the depth of learning a person's tells in a fighting game and bonding with them through the exchanging of blows. ALSO IT'S FREE- a game with this much depth and replayability with good co-op and it's free? Even if you just see it as an occasional party game w/ friends, this is some FANTASTIC funny e-sports air hockey.

Omega strikers is a wonderful game. It's interesting with fun characters and fun gameplay. I instantly fell in love with the game and sank many hours into it. However, I think the devs bit off more than they could chew. They threw it onto too many platforms and made many other poor decisions and I think stretched themselves out too thin. Spreading themselves out so thin with such a small dev team led to too many problems. Many bugs that have gone unsolved for example. Their marketing was questionable and their monetization of the game was abysmal. It's absolutely zero surprise they aren't making money on the game when there's almost nothing to buy within the game. There's the occasional season pass and a handful of skins. That's it. There's nothing to even buy with the normal free currency. A massive complaint people have is that there's literally nothing to spend the credits and style points on after a certain point. There were many options for monetization they could have taken without going for a p2w model or anything. They were even releasing characters without any skins. They were told by multiple people that the major problems were the onboarding and the matchmaking. Matchmaking was somewhat understandably hard to fix due to the low player counts but the mm for normals and quickplay made the onboarding problem worse. The onboarding is abysmal in this game. The tutorial is not good and doesn't teach everything. Then after doing it the new players are thrown in to pick a mode. The options are ranked, quick play, and normals. Ranked sounds scary and obviously someone new to the game probably isn't going to gravitate to it so they're likely to go with quickplay or normal. The problem with that is quickplay and normal had ZERO matchmaking. So you'd have new players getting put up against long time players that are way better than them and then being toxic at them for being so bad when they're just new. I can't blame people for not wanting to sink in the hours to eventually learn the game when that's their first impression of it. The devs were told multiple times they needed to shift their priorities away from these constant micro balance patches and strange choices like the summer visual novel event but they dug their heads into the sand and marched on. The devs have just given up at the sign that the game is failing and whined about the reasoning being because of money(again, big shocker when the game is basically not monetized at all). Them not even lasting a year before just giving up and abandoning the game does not spark hope in me that their next game will be a success or that they'd stick with it.

Overall I love this game and would certainly recommend it(I managed to suck in 4 of my friends into playing and liking the game).but the constant untouched problems and now the devs just giving up has left a sour aftertaste for me so I'm leaving this as a negative review which makes me sad but I still hope that their next game is good and does well.

UPDATE:

If you like simple competitive games, air hockey, and varied characters and moba-style abilities you'll probably like this game. Unfortunately, Odyssey Interactive is focused on creating new games, and this one is maintained by only one or two individuals while we wait for the next release.

Despite this, the game is still very playable, and some minor content updates do still come every once in a while.

Gameplay is fairly straightforward, with a goalie and two forwards on each team. Players select the role they wish to play before queuing, guaranteeing that you'll get the role you actually want (though there is some nuance in that forwards have two primary positions and you may not get to play forward the way you want to). Characters in Ranked modes are selected in draft/ban fashion not unlike any other MOBA, with one overall ban per team chosen randomly out of each players' votes.

As you might expect, the difference between ranked play and normal matches is completely different, with the skill level of most ranked players being much higher (and in many cases lower) than players that stick to Normals. For this reason I often recommend new players stick with the Normal or Quick Play modes until they're comfortable scoring or defending in their particular role and choice of Striker.

Overall, it's a good game. I've been playing on and off since the Alpha test and I've loved it all the way. It's a shame we don't get a lot of new content, but what's there is enough to keep it somewhat fresh between seasons.

This is up there for being the best competitive game of all time. It's only issue... the lack of players.

With infinite depth by team compositions, awakening draft, and strategies that can only be effective on certain maps, Omega Strikers has an incredibly high skill ceiling. Passing plays between teammates feels amazing, KO'ing players off the side of the map is always rewarding. But, circling back to the issue, the lack of players, for NA West players, it might be difficult to find matches of acceptable latency. Anything above 60 ping is borderline unplayable due to human reaction times, and many of the games can be found on US East servers (92+ for me). If there were more players on the west coast (or in general), I would give this game a perfect score.

However, I'd rate Omega Strikers a 10/10 for gameplay, and a 8/10 with the lack of players. Although development is now paused as Odyssey work on a more profitable game, I hope this game can retain more players that last longer than two weeks.

Omega Strikers was a very fun, cool and unique game to play based on concept and originality however, the games potential got squandered throughout the process as time went on due to incompetent decisions, developers biting off more than they could chew and then the mediocre patch notes in which the players had addressed issues with bugs, gameplay balance issues. 

This game could've lasted a lot longer had it not suffered said issues at hand and as someone who's not into MOBA, I really did enjoy Omega Strikers but unfortunately, the state it's in is wasted potential at this point and to put the nail in the coffin, the developers have 'pulled the plug' on this game. Yes, the game could go on but they're not really adding much else to the game. 

The two main reasons that drew me into the game were the animation opening done by Studio TRIGGER and then I saw this game on one of the Nintendo showcases live stream one day, and it gauged my interest. 

Having played the game for a while, it did start to get fairly repetitive for me but thankfully there were cases in which you could experiment with any character in game and see what was best fit for the players needs. HOWEVER, this game could've had a practice mode from the start or a little after it launched rather than throwing the player into the deep end by playing multiplayer only. Also, there were times in which the match making was awful. Sometimes waiting for a game/match would take up to 10 minutes, in my experience. 

In conclusion, I really wanted to love Omega Strikers and thought the game would go on for a long time. Concept, premise, uniqueness, characters, presentation it was all there but as time went on that potential crumbled and then, having read the games patch notes and how the PR was addressing the game, it felt out of touch. It really is a shame, hopefully whatever Odyssey Interactive's next game will be, they will learn from their mistakes and improvise with their next game.

I love this game so much and it pains me to hear the recent announcement of no more new content, I felt like I must write a review.

Omega Strikers is possibly the best multiplayer game out right now with its unique take of air hockey by combining it with MOBA elements. Its fast-paced competitive gameplay is addicting and every match plays incredibly different so the game has good replayability because of the game's "awakening system" where you are given eight choices to build your character which very much reminds me of a rogue-like or league of legends with its items. The developers, Odyssey Interactive, are also very active in the community as well as treating the community, content creators, and everyone on their team. They even got to collab with Studio Trigger to make an animated opening of their game. As awesome as this game is, the game still struggled to retain their playerbase leading to a stagnation in the expected growth of the game. I hate to be the one to say it, but there are a lot of issues with the game that made it very difficult for new players to get into Omega Strikers. The ones I find most crucial are:

[h1]1. User Experience:[/h1]
While the game is very beginner-friendly with a high skill ceiling, it has a terrible tutorial that doesn't teach anything, a lot of players like myself had to play against players with more experience which makes it difficult to learn the game. Thankfully, the community is very helpful with guides and videos that better explain the game that helped me learn and understand the game. But the game relying on the community to provide information to the players makes it feel like a chore to learn the game. Not many want to go out of their way to learn a game they're not invested in because they don't understand it.

[h1]2. Communication:[/h1]
For a team-based game, the lack of communication really hurts this game a lot. The communication is limited to just 7 call outs(it used to be 5). While they are useful, it doesn't help new players very much. The developers refuse to add any type of chat system because they want to prevent toxicity but that locks out a lot of people from helping new players mid-game. Because of this, people will make mistakes and there are no tools to positively correct them which makes it stressful and frustrating for experienced players.


[h1]3. Balancing/Map Design:[/h1]
The game is definitely balanced. However the developers were really unsure if they wanted to make this a competitive game or a party game. This is very clear and evident through the questionable balance changes. Such as the constant nerfs to a character named Asher in the past few months. The map designs are also very good but if you take a look at the earlier maps and the newer maps, you do notice a change in design philosophy. Older maps are very straight-forward with a simple mechanic added to spice things up between them. An example I can give is a map called "Oni Village" which has speed lanes on the top and bottom of the map which helps repositioning as it speeds up the players and the balls. There's also "Ai.mi's App" which is your average map design but it has a hole in the middle which counts as a Knockout Edge. The hole is very unique and versatile as it can be used to KO your opponents or you can use it as a wall to create interesting dribbles/passes. Then we look at a map like "Gates of Obscura" which is a huge map with large portals that teleports both players and the ball. Which isn't a problem but the portals are randomized with every round and the map makes the game feel more like a RNG party game. You can see the change in map design philosophy and it shows that the developers were unsure if they wanted to go for a party game or competitive game route. 

No matter the decisions of the developers, I will still love this game. But I want them to understand the many criticisms that this game receives. The devs are good at taking criticisms, their discord has a feedback tab and they listen to their players. But for some reason, a lot of these criticisms (mostly the first two I mentioned) are disregarded. Despite my criticisms of the game, I want [b]YOU[/b] to play the game if you haven't. And if you have, I want [b]YOU[/b] to keep on playing whether you are new or not. Keep on grinding to get good at this game, I promise its worth it because Omega Strikers is the most satisfying multiplayer game ever. 

[i]If you need a guide to this game, look up[/i] [b]"How 2 Not Suck at Omega Strikers"[/b]
