Omega Strikers is a fun 3v3 Sports MOBA that is unfortunately plagued by it's own niche.

It is deceptively difficult to pick up (just hitting the core and positioning are 2 things most people will struggle for the first 50 hours) so beginners are either eager to learn but get stomped by veterans or get discouraged in the first place due to the confusion of what's generally happening.

The fast-paced gameplay paired with the 1.0 release system of slowing the game down with intermissions and splitting the game between a Best of 5 Rounds within a Best of 5 Sets system just made the game feel like a fast paced highway followed by a left turn with traffic waiting for the next joyride and every game can either feel exhausting or straight up frustrating.

The Awakenings System(TM)
Possibly the worst system I have ever encountered that acts as the main Ranked game mode.
What's the problem with it?

The Worst of Both Worlds
For Casuals:
Not only are you expected to know what awakenings are good for your strikers, you're also expected to know which ones you should deny no matter what from the opposing side, leading to beginners having a stroke because they're immediately met with a knowledge check during the intermission after being confused about the game flow.

For Experienced Players:
Not only is the system completely RNG but the boon of "not every game is the same" is met with "Everyone's performance will vary per game". You can play like a god and miss out on awakenings you do want anyways due to picking up a Spark on set 2 and never seeing another one again until set 5. You can see GonzalesForward dominating with the best in slot awakenings for his character in one game and then struggle to hit that high on the next.

Balancing Issues:
The awakening system is flawed because everyone can't get what they want consistently so they work on numbers that are flawed in the first place. Is the Juliette taking the useless Monumentalist because it's good or is it because Juliette is forced to take it away from the opposing Nao? Basic stuff like that is negligible but when you start considering problematic awakenings that are often misunderstood by the community (Deadeye), it will stay overtuned and underpicked due to people not understanding how short of a range 500 actually is, because the game never tells you what 500 range actually is. Not to mention awakenings that are absurdly strong on certain characters but subpar on everyone else is also a very tricky balancing bar that leads to some changes that leaves certain circles within the community baffled.

TLDR to all of this, This game is fun and give it a shot. I listed all the flaws I personally dislike about this game but that's okay. Beginners can take their time to learn but just know, our community is small as it is and if you're not ready to see similar faces everyday, especially in the Asia community, it can't be helped.

I want to enjoy this game, and I will keep playing it, however a few things are keeping me from recommending this game.
Firstly is the matchmaking, my god its not even funny how unbalanced it feels at times with the way teams are stacked up, do yourself a favor and avoid normal mode like the plague until you have at least 30-50 hours in the game. The mode itself is comp but you don't have a ban phase, which sounds fine but the matches take much longer then quick play, give slightly better rewards (if you win) and overall feel helpless if your getting stomped (which as a new player you absolutely will be).
I feel this problem is due to a lack of newer players coming in, and veterans having so much more experience that they can exploit often overlooked mechanics and abilities, sure with time you can get the hang of this, but if I wanted to get stomped playing a Moba I would go back to league...

Secondly, the balancing... Now let me preface this point by saying the balancing is fairly tight all things considered and you can certainly do well with every character out there, but my god to some characters feel like straight up grades to others. Also this game has hard counters based on play-style alone and let me tell you, the game does not disclose this or tell you how to deal with it. You just gotta figure that ♥♥♥♥ out on your own.

Third is well, the grind. You don't get a lot of points per match (about 900 a game for quickplay) which is alright, but characters range in cost from 10k to 30k to 50k, which is a lot of matches that can feel really bad when point 1 comes in to play. Sure on account level you get 5k points and getting a characters rank to 2 gives you 3k per character, but even still it feels dismally slow when games don't feel fun to play and your trying desperately to find one character that might make things less painful.

I want to like this game, the artstyle, the emotes, and the community are all really nice. But as it stands right now I can only stand a game or two before matchmaking puts me on the loss streak and reminds me "yeah no this is why I dislike competitive games."

I've listened to countless guides and spent quite a bit of time learning the ropes and trying to get better, but I feel like I'm fighting a uphill battle when I can have more fun elsewhere with less of a headache. :/

This game is the most enjoyable competitive game I've ever played.

Matches aren't too long or short, getting into a game is quick, you are almost ALWAYS spending your time doing actual gameplay with little downtime, and it always feels like you have agency despite being one player on a team.

I don't think I've played a competitive game that has literally been an enjoyable experience in almost every aspect that makes it "competitive".

Above all else, its incredibly impressive how this game is able to appeal to both competitive "I want to get better" players and casual "play for fun" players.

The learning curve of this game is probably the best i've seen in the genre. The mechanics are simple and easy to understand, yet the game has so much room for depth and skill expression. The new player experience is incredibly enjoyable, as you try to figure out and experiment the nuances of the game's simple mechanics and how to manipulate them to your advantage. 

The character design and "balancing" of this game is also top-notch. Balance can be a very controversial subject in competitive games, but I am a firm believer that this game has the best approach to it. Speaking from personal experience, even characters that are perceived as "weak" by most people are still very much viable and can be taken to the higher brackets. If I had to make an analogy, Omega strikers feels less like rock-paper-scissors, where one character will counter another, and more like chess, where there is room for counterplay rather than a direct "hard counter".

Overall, I love this game, I hope to see it have a bright future, it is one of the rare competitive games where I never ended up questioning why I wasted my time. It is one of the rare competitive games I actually grinded ranked soloQ and had fun.

I like this game. It's a fun game.

But. Luck does not make it fun.

It needs a gameplay change. Normal/Ranked item selection.

Buffs/items are given out exclusively to players via an order system based on score/contribution, meaning that players who do well are given first pick for whatever item they want and last-pick players are, well, last pick for sucking dong.

Say for example, you deal with a team who focuses more on bruiser/KOing. They target you. You can't contribute because you're dead all of the time. That's not necessarily a problem with the game or anything, it's just a playstyle that works. BUT. Omega Strikers rotates the items in and out. No Stagger Swagger, no Unstoppable? You can't get the defensive items because they're being rotated out in an attempt to change meta and force people to stop one-tricking? You're screwed, and your team is basically forced to deal with a teammate that's only suboptimal at best.

Woah, the enemy team's Octavia is now super speedy because she got lucky with all the right items! But you got unlucky and you haven't been able to get a single item that could help in punishing her! Actually, no one could! Because the other team took them all! Because their enemy team snowballed from the top of Mount ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ all the way down to Noob-Slope.

Now you're last pick and you have to suffer the game picking items you don't want to have because the player you're going up against is beating whatever playstyle you COULD'VE had because of a combination of superior skill and items better suited for, unfortunately, that same playstyle. I don't like this concept of luck being a skill issue in what is essentially a soccer game.

It's a silly idea to me to make this a "ball-chase, first pick" system. Personally, I don't think there should be a "score" system at all, because you're encouraging certain play styles and essentially discouraging being a passer or a support, instead encouraging KO's and goals. If you wanted to really explore playstyles without the game punishing you for being more passive, you should just let everyone pick whatever items they want. I wouldn't bring back the mastery system from the beta, I would keep the item system and just give everyone free reign over the items. People are going to one-trick regardless of what the game throws at them, but at least this makes it fair for everyone who's actually trying to play. 

Seriously, I would take any system over what Omega Strikers has. Like:
- Maintain the stat-order system, but allow the top three or two players to pick any item they want regardless of what it is. Whatever items are picked will not be available for the last three/two, unless they're in the same team. The last three/two picks any item they want out of the selection. It'll encourage playing better, but it won't drastically punish bottom scorers for either playing like crap or getting bullied to hell.
- Remove the system entirely, allow all players free reign over items out of the selection. It'll encourage one-tricking, but now the game is entirely fairplay and "skill issue." If you got beaten at your own game, it's good opportunity to study up on how to better your playstyle.
- Pity system. Last player gets access to two or three other items on the selection that are exclusive to them. Doesn't have to be specific. I played through the beta, and put around 25 hours into it with another friend of mine.  Once the game shutdown in preparation for the full release, I kind of forgot about it.  But after almost 5 months, the game finally released, and I was very excited.

First, for the perspective of a new player, the game is awesome.  A 3v3 air hockey game with elements of MOBA games.  I've heard it be described as "Rocket League of Legends", and that is spot on.  You coordinate with your team to get past 2 player acting as attackers (called forwards) and then outsmart a third player as a goalie.  At the time of writing this review, there are 17 playable characters (only 4 unlocked at first), all of which are very unique.  The visuals are great, the character designs are splendid, and the music is ironically stupid with how good it is.  Most character abilities feel balanced and fair to use, but this games get constant updates so the devs are always fine tuning the experience.

Now the perspective for those who played beta,
I understand why there are lots of disagreements.  I do kinda miss the old gear system, but I also enjoy the variety of the new awakenings.  And there are a lot more improvements made to the full release that I fell make the game better.  But even if you have the things you hate or dislike, the core theme, idea, vibe, and enjoyment factor has not changed.

In total, this game is very fun.  I've convinced some of my friends to play, and those who stuck with it love it.  Its a free game, and its not a big one at that, so getting someone to check it out isn't hard.  The competitive scene is great, there's plenty of options to help you get used to the game mechanics, and overall is so worth it.  Everything in the game you can purchase with real cash is either cosmetics, emotes, or a battle pass which is full of player titles, player cards, more emotes, and more cosmetics.  This game has no pay to win, which makes it satisfying to pull off a victory.  Its skill based, and the best players are the best for a reason.

If you are reading this and you haven given this game a chance, then just do it.  If you don't like it, then don't play it.  But if you do like it, you'll start your new addiction.

Omega Strikers: A Harrowing Spiral into Mediocrity

In the shadows of the gaming industry, where creativity and innovation are meant to thrive, Omega Strikers emerges as a lackluster addition to the genre. As a self-proclaimed Danganronpa-inspired experience, it falls short of capturing the essence that made its predecessor so beloved. Prepare for a descent into despair as we dissect the game's flaws and missed opportunities.

From the outset, it becomes apparent that Omega Strikers lacks the gripping narrative and compelling characters that defined Danganronpa. The story, a feeble attempt at replicating the dark and twisted atmosphere, comes off as a cheap imitation. The attempts at creating suspense and mystery are shallow, failing to evoke the same level of intrigue and investment.

The characters, too, are disappointingly one-dimensional. Gone are the complex and morally ambiguous personalities that made Danganronpa a standout. Instead, we are presented with a forgettable cast of archetypal individuals who lack depth and fail to engage the player on an emotional level. The attempts at injecting romantic elements feel forced and uninspired, doing little to enhance the overall experience.

Gameplay-wise, Omega Strikers stumbles even further. The mechanics feel clunky and poorly executed, with repetitive and uninspired combat sequences that quickly become tiresome. The game fails to offer any meaningful strategic depth, leaving players longing for the engaging trials and investigations that made Danganronpa so captivating. The puzzle elements, once a hallmark of the series, are reduced to simplistic and unchallenging tasks that provide little satisfaction.

Visually, Omega Strikers lacks the polish and attention to detail that fans have come to expect. The environments are bland and uninspiring, lacking the vibrant and immersive settings that characterized Danganronpa. The art style, though reminiscent of its predecessor, fails to capture the same level of artistry and creativity, leaving players longing for the unique aesthetics that defined the original series.

Furthermore, the sound design of Omega Strikers leaves much to be desired. The lackluster soundtrack fails to create the atmospheric tension necessary to immerse players in its world. The voice acting, often wooden and lacking emotion, fails to breathe life into the characters, further exacerbating the disconnect between the player and the game.

In the end, Omega Strikers falls victim to its own aspirations. By attempting to ride the coattails of Danganronpa's success, it only highlights its own shortcomings. The lackluster narrative, forgettable characters, uninspired gameplay, and underwhelming presentation all contribute to an experience that fails to live up to its lofty ambitions.

For fans of Danganronpa seeking a worthy successor, Omega Strikers will leave you disheartened and longing for the brilliance of its predecessor. It serves as a reminder that attempting to replicate the magic of a beloved franchise is no easy feat, and in this case, it falls short, leaving players with a bitter taste of disappointment.

Alright, listen up fellow gamers because this is the single greatest game I've played in a LONG time. First I'll talk about the gameplay, then credits, then the humor, and then the devs. 

tl;dr this game reignited my hope that good games can still be made and words cannot describe how good this game is. (numbers can tho, 10 outta 10 would greatly recommend.)

[b]Gameplay[/b]

Alright, first of all, the gameplay is [i]SMOOTH[/i]. Excluding mobile (ofc) the controls are super easy to grasp and really friendly to the gamer. I personally use WASD to move around, but if you come from League or Starcraft, I understand using the mouse pointer to move. To say which mode of transportation is superior is purely subjective, in truth it's which ever you're more comfortable with and what you have a history in. All and all tho, all characters are fun to play and the abilities are quick and easy to understand. I wish there was a way to know how character abilities work before purchasing them rather than just reading a summary of the ability, but that's just a nit pick. 

[b]Currency[/b] 

First, it's SUPER easy to get enough credits to buy new characters. It feels fair and doesn't require a HUGE grind to get all the characters you want. I can tell here and in many other cases that the Devs prioritized the consumers needs over any scummy tactics they could have employed like many companies do (Overwatch is a good example). The currency seems fair for what you're buying and when I spend money on the game. Even if you buy in-game currency with real money, you get a LOT of it and it really feels like the Devs don't want your money, but rather for you to have a fun time playing there game which I REALLY respect, but I'll talk more on that later.

[b]Humor[/b]

The humor is some of the most wholesome I've encountered in so long. Instead of an in-game chat, players can communicate with emotes instead, mostly just for messing around and by golly are the emotes PERFECT. First, they're based off of well known memes which already makes me giddy, but they aren't just copy and pasted off the internet, they re-drawings of memes of their characters WHICH IS EVEN MORE HILARIOUS! I've seen some really unique uses of the emotes that made me really laugh out loud while playing which I hadn't laughed so much playing a game for the longest time. The emotes, while being really funny, are a quick form of communication that provides an alternate to in game chat messages which is another aspect I love. You can only chat with the enemy team through the uses of emotes, which are mostly memes, which leads to really really really wholesome interactions with your supposed enemies. Despite this being a PvP game, it still sometimes feels like you're playing with a bunch of friends just here to have a good time. The emotes provide humor as well as friendly communication with supposed enemies turning all of this into a good time.

[b]Devs[/b]

Please notice me Devs, I love you guys ❤️from what I understand, and please correct me if I am incorrect, but the Devs originally worked on League of Legends, but didn't like the direction the game was going with its toxicity, huge grind, and unfair in-game currency. So they split off and decided to make a new (and better IMO) game that fixed all the problems that they saw League has. In turn, they created a masterpiece that isn't a money grab but rather seems like a passion project aimed for making a game that both the Devs and the player base loves. The Devs are also just really funny, from the great decision to add meme emotes to the game, to the fact they had Nevercake (a popular youtube animator) create an ad for the game that perfectly and hilariously sums up the game and it's frankly the perfect kind of ad you'll ever see, especially for a game like Omega Strikers. Here's a link to the ad (and it feels less like an ad and more of a video you would optionally watch if you'd see it on your recommended. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pHjg-gYlLTU
The Devs are overall the gigest of giga chads and it really makes me happy they're so connected with the community and knows what's right for the game and it makes you feel like the Devs are actual good people.

You know what, this game really has a lot of potential. The artstyle is a huge plus in my book, I love games with stylized graphics. It'll make it so it'll never really age. When it comes to the gameplay, ♥♥♥♥'s addicting. A neutron activates  in my brain every time the ball goes back and forth faster and faster. I will say there's literally no way for me to understand EVERY mechanic in the game or what item works on what, but at the same time you can just pick whatever and roll. A minor complaint I have is the lack of role suggestion. I'd like if it was shown on the character's summery if they're more so geared to play in the goal or on the field. Every character has a unique playstyle and I like that a lot. The slime girl is really focused on setting up for trickshots or a lot of pressure. The girl with a ponytail and red highlights (I don't remember everyone's name just yet) seems to me like a type of character that is a lot more focused on fighting the other team. The fighting can be very annoying, especially when you can tell someone's clearly targeting you. It's like they're not even focusing on the core. Game also works wonders on ♥♥♥♥♥♥ internet, I dunno how the devs did that honestly. I've seen some people ask for a training mode, which well, would be pretty sweet to learn character abilities in a controlled environment. It also took me a bit to understand how the Q ability works properly... I don't know if I just didn't pay enough attention or the explanation wasn't clear enough. Oh yeah there's a lot of things the game throws at you and it CAN be a bit overwhelming, especially with the huge block of text. My suggestion would be to direct the player with an arrow or something to a tutorial that's voiced by a character. Yeah, that'd cost more money but me personally, it's easier to invest in it when I'm being talked to, rather than having to read a whole bunch. F2P game means cosmetics are the main way to monetize the game. I don't mind that at all, and the battle pass isn't bad looking either. I'm not exactly sure but if you play for long enough I think you can obtain it for free. Rewarding dedication is really good! And it doesn't hurt spending players because they can use it on other cosmetics, emotes, etc. The art team also killed it when it came to the emotes. At least I think the art team was behind it anyway. Genuinely cute and funny. Also thanks for not having a chat feature, that was a good call in this instance.  

The developers also seem to be very active and reply to reviews, be it ones with memes, critical ones (I'm super happy to see they read them and take it in consideration) and just positive ones too. I feel like this game could get really far and have it's own niche audience. Having it F2P is a huge W for introducing new players, it's easier for the community to grow too. I usually don't write reviews this long because the games I buy/play often I feel like don't need a huge review, but seeing as Omega Strikers is still starting out it might be valuable for the devs and everyone working on this product. I also managed to find this game by word of mouth, so that's good. There's a mobile version of the game as well, it's rated 3.6* in the Android Store, though I'm not sure if its because of its instability or because the demographic of mobile players VS PC players is just incredibly different. I swear some of the mobile app reviews make me question if we're using the same app sometimes...

Overall, Omega Strikers is amazing fun especially with friends. Now, if you play solo like I do sometimes it might not be as fun. I've also had issues where I'm paired with less experienced players on my team, versing people who've played for a whole lot longer than me. Maybe matchmaking needs to be looked into but at the very least I'm thankful that the matches are quick to find. More game is better than waiting in que! I also am not surprised if the playerbase of League Of Legends overlaps a bit with this one, I've seen some very stupid people either just stay in a corner or refuse to play, or even straight up disconnecting. I've had a match where both my teammates disconnected on me. The enemy team felt so bad, that one of them playing as the mechanic small woman with dark hair decided to flat out just play on my side of the field. We had some fun before they just, let me win. 

So that's the both sides of the Omega Strikers community, the duality if you will. Oh one last thing, I usually avoid mobas for this exact reason but, I really don't like rooting, silencing and mechanics like that. So please in the future keep this in mind, as I don't want the game to become a stunfest. Omega Striker looks the coolest and is at its most fun when both teams push with the core with some bashing every now and then. Would recommend giving it a shot at least! I mean, the game's free. The most you could lose is like, an hour of your time.

For a more in-depth description, Omega Strikers takes a lot of basic components of a MOBA and combines them with... air hockey, of all things. Your objective is to work with your team to hit the other team's barriers with the Core/ball/puck/whatever the hell you want to call it so their goal opens up and you can score a point while preventing the other team from doing the same to you. Games are either first to 5 points (Coop vs AI and Quick Play) or first to win 3 3-point sets (Normals and Competitive). Instead of a typical health bar, you have a Stagger bar that works kinda like percentage in Super Smash Bros; the lower your Stagger is, the easier you are to knock around and hit into the edges of the arena, which leaves you waiting to respawn after about twelve seconds. Each character has a set of abilities that facilitates their own playstyle, it's 2023, we all know how MOBAs work at this point. That being said, I think this game can go far if Odyssey plays their cards right.

I'm playing Omega Strikers because it's F2P and it's got a lot of promise as a game to play with friends, but it has some glaring issues that need to be sorted out before I can recommend it.

First, a more minor grievance, the fact that "Normal" mode matches take SO LONG makes having a losing streak feel HORRIBLE, yet they are objectively the more engaging game type to play, because of the way you get to make a character build as you play. This is just frustrating. I am ready to sit and play for a whole night, but my friends get two losses in, and they're burnt out.

Second, what has bugged me far more, the way the "Normal" mode system works with the character buffs you get between rounds is absolutely counter-intuitive to competitive gameplay. The players with higher stats get first-pick, causing horrendous snowballing that's effectively impossible to recover from. This mechanic would serve as such a good balancing mechanic if the players who performed low got to even the odds by having a more synergistic build. THIS might make the length of the game feel better, as you'd at least have better opportunities to score some rounds, even if you don't win the set.

Third, Quickplay could implement some form of augment drafting to make shorter matches still feel more engaging, and less random. The randomized buffs just flat-out occasionally benefit specific characters more, so the idea that randomizing it and everybody gets the same set doesn't make for a balanced drop-in-and-play mode. While I'd prefer some level of quick-picking or draft votes, it'd be better than the current way they have it if they just removed the buffs from quickplay altogether. What is currently there is a compromise that doesn't work.

I would like to be able to recommend this game, I wish I could, as it is charming, and I want to like it, but it is tripping over its own feet by trying to expand its content before focusing down on the core experience. Character balance also seems dubious, but I don't have unbiased data to support that.

- Don't confuse it with soccer; there are no aerial balls. It would be more like air hockey.
- There seem to be characters that are unbalanced, but since the focus is not on eliminating opponents like in Smash Bros or Dota, the game has another layer of balance, where those who can dominate the ball (or puck) have a greater impact on the game.

- The UI system needs some improvement. In-game, there is an urgent need for a surrender option. It gets frustrating to have to play 3 sets when one or more players have quit the game.

TLDR: This is a fun brawler/air hockey MOBA that could use some minor tweaks such as a forfeit option and a couple extra emoticons, but is otherwise fun and enjoyable and worth giving a try, especially since it is free to play.

UPDATE: They added a forfeit option, but the entire team must agree. I wish it was majority rules, but I'm ultimately grateful for any forfeit option.

This game is a perfect, (mostly) non-toxic alternative to League of Legends, a popular MOBA. This game is essentially air hockey, but with added brawling and abilities that vary for each character option (Striker) to use on yourself, others or the core (the puck). There are 3 sets, and the first to score 3 goals wins the set. And the first team to win 3 sets wins the entire match. Between each set, you get to select items or "Awakenings" that improve your Striker's abilities. The better you perform in the previous set, the more likely you are to get to pick first before other players. And you better be able to get to the Awakening you want first, as the majority of them can only be selected by one player, minus one Awakening that can be chosen by anyone no matter other player's choices before you; all potential Awakenings are randomized each time. In competitive, you get the added bonus of getting the opportunity to ban a Striker from the match so that no one, even people on your team, can play as them, but it is otherwise the same in normal mode. 

You get a small selection of Strikers to begin with, but just from playing the game, you can unlock everyone, although it is not necessary. I personally took my time in unlocking everyone after I found my favorite couple to play. There are quite a few to choose from and each has a different play style and different abilities. You'll pick up on which Awakenings work best for which Strikers, and there are guides and suggestions online if you need them.

In addition, the game is free, unless you want to purchase cosmetics or unlock all of the characters faster. Other than being able to be more flexible in character selection, paying money does not equal winning or any additional upper hand which I appreciate.

This game does not have a voice or text chat feature, which I am in love with. Instead, players can only use pre-designed emoticons, and there is quite a range of them. It is so much better to the alternative of people screaming obscenities and threatening violence over a game. However, I wish I could more directly tell my teammates a bigger variety of things (for example, there is no way to tell your goalie to stay in the goal when they start to wander too far). And of course you have people spamming them and some of the emoticons have grown to have mean implications, but that's easy to get over and overall I prefer it this way rather than the traditional voice/text chat.

However, they do need to include a forfeit/concede option, which I'm baffled doesn't already exist. I have had an unfortunate amount of matches where frustrated players exit the game and as it stands now, the game does not end after one or two players leave, nor does it auto-fill with more players, even in Normal mode. In my eyes, this is a huge design flaw. Players either start to play for the opposite team to make the match even (which I can respect the idea of, but it can be frustrating when you are trying to complete missions and want to win) or the last player standing has to wait through the rest of the match just to lose. It's a crazy oversight to not expect people to rage quit or for people to have bad internet connections. BUT, I'd say the majority of the time this isn't a problem. It is just painfully annoying/frustrating when it happens.

Besides that, if you enjoy this genre and type of game, you'll enjoy Omega Strikers. Honestly, MOBAs aren't typically my type of game but clearly I'm addicted. I absolutely recommend trying it out and get some friends to play too!

Great football/hockey game with MOBA like controls and abilities. With the latest patches there's also a lot of map and character variety. There's not much to improve except for a chat feature.

I'm not a fan of MOBA games, but this definitely makes for an exception. Probably because I don't really have to play it as a MOBA.

Having no chat during the game I think is a wise decision. There is still some quick chat that allows for some basic communication, and some fun emotes that borrow from memes and highly used Twitch emotes that help them feel contemporary. Traditional text party chat is in the main menu, so it's not entirely limited, but keeping communication this short I think helps keep the focus on the game.

Characters are very distinct in playstyle, their artwork and design look great, and are all earned just by playing the game. The characters available at the start are on par with others unlocked later, each powerful in their own right. Knowing this game was made by former League of Legends Developers, and seeing that every character is this capable to do well in any given match, meaning success hinges more on the skill of the player and not so much the choice of character is encouraging. Well, except that brief time once Vyce and Octavia were released, but that situation was rectified inside a day. Hopefully characters released later on are kept in this balance as much as possible, though it is known in League that new characters released tend to have a period where they excel because no one knows how to counterplay them, and I expect no different here, but focusing counterplay on playstyle vs. playstyle rather than character vs. character I think is a better way to go in the long run.

The cosmetics include skins (that can also change how your abilities appear), goal explosions, and player card backgrounds, beyond the previously mentioned emotes. Some are exclusively for Cash Credits (here being "Ody Coins"), some earned through a battle pass, affinities, and leveling up your account, and others through "Style Points," also earned through those systems. Cash Credits can be used to unlock other characters and items ordinarily costing Style points, if you wish, and of course upgrade your pass to a premium version for more goodies. Anything that might affect gameplay, barring the strikers, are not for sale: you do not have to buy the items for them to appear during gameplay.

The graphical demands of this game are relatively light, making it easy to keep framerates high even on lower-end and older machines, making this game very accessible. Such a stylized appearance might put off some, but as we see in games like this, Valorant, and yes, Mihoyo's lineup, the game overall can still look good without high-resolution textures or high polycount models. As a result, the game can be played, and is available, on just about everything, with crossplay.

There are also attempts to keep the game feeling fresh. Recently the available items and courts in ranked play have been slightly changed. At release, the courts were radically changed to include the barriers that block the goals, which I think helped the defensive side get a better fighting chance, where beta footage shows the goal gates slowly opening over the first twenty seconds or so of the round. I hope to see other court gimmicks like these later on, but even this kind of gameplay still feels good, especially on the competitive side.

The control scheme does require some mention, as you can choose between a MOBA style and traditional WASD. You can play this as you would League, but since you will be put in situations where you need to move one direction but strike the puck in another, WASD is said to be superior. I will echo this sentiment: too many times have I seen a player obviously playing with MOBA controls strike the puck into their own goal. Unless you have won a televised League of Legends Tournament, do not use MOBA controls, or you WILL, I repeat, WILL self-goal, among other blunders.

As a far less complicated MOBA than League of Legends, and with gameplay objectives and methods clear for all to see, I think this game stands a chance to get the E-Sports spot that Odysee is going for. There seems to be always some kind of competition going on, between the Creator Vs. event at its release, the Pro League Invitational, and now the almost Splatoon-style Demon Duel with another Creator Vs. on the way. The game is easy to get into and understand, and with the playerbase this large there will always be people to queue up and play with and against you. Hop in and get ready, your favorite creators will probably need your help!

Have you ever played league of legends? If so my condolences; but unlike league of legends this is fun.
Have you ever played soccer? I haven't, but I have watched Blue Lock; it's pretty good.

Omega Strikers is luckily, not like league of legends, and "technically" more like air hockey than soccer, that doesn't matter... When I hit goals I just feel like "that guy", I become an egoist, I am "him", I'm able to analyse the field with utmost precision and skill; whenever I miss goals, or self goal by accident or misplay in any capacity, I'm "washed", "dogwater" and "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrible". I don't know if I'm bipolar, but what I do know is that nonetheless this game is fun as hell.

The gameplay is something that I thought would get boring pretty quickly, but it's just a solid experience overall. The gameplay is casual, but has enough depth for it to get competitive. Stages and awakenings(random power ups you choose at the start of the game) keep the game fresh, while the base gameplay feels satisfying. Most characters seem well defined by their kits with clear strengths and weaknesses, I think the game is mostly balanced. 

Funny things about the game is that there's no ingame voice chat or text chat, which is for the best; but this game is also way better with friends for that very reason.

Another funny thing about this game is that I have no idea how many games and genres Omega Striker devs looked at when making the game, because awakenings remind me of roguelikes, characters remind me of overwatch, top down gameplay reminds me of mobas, and combat reminds me somewhat of super smash bros; in any case, it just works.

In terms of monetization practices, I think the game is pretty fair as well since you can get all the characters for free, and there's missions for stuff too.

Other things to end the review off is that 
A.) The style / art direction for this game is good, I like the designs.

B.) I will say some stages feel slightly small at times.

C.) Playing with people who don't quite understand the game makes me internally cry in pain, but I'm also happy I can't outplay an entire team consistently as a single player, a part of the experience is the team based gameplay after all.

D.) I pray this game never gets too competitive, or too casual; the balance between competitive and casual gameplay is hard to achieve, but at least right now the game feels like it doesn't lean heavily in either direction (although I haven't yet tried ranked)

"Boku no Heya ga Dungeon no Kyuukeijo ni Natteshimatta Ken," also known as "My Room Has Become a Dungeon Rest Stop," is a manga series written by Tougoku Hudou and illustrated by Takoyakiyoshi.

The story revolves around Yuuji Sano, a young man who has always been a homebody and prefers spending his time indoors. One day, inexplicably, Yuuji's room transforms into a mysterious dungeon. The room becomes a gateway to a vast underground world filled with monsters, treasures, and adventurers.

As Yuuji tries to make sense of this bizarre transformation, he encounters a girl named Ria, who happens to be an adventurer. Ria explains that Yuuji's room has become a "rest stop" for adventurers, a safe haven where they can rest, heal, and resupply before venturing further into the dangerous dungeon.

Realizing that he now has a significant role to play, Yuuji reluctantly takes on the responsibility of managing the rest stop. With Ria's guidance, he learns to navigate the intricacies of the dungeon and assist the weary adventurers who seek refuge in his room.

As time goes on, Yuuji's understanding of the dungeon deepens, and he begins to uncover the secrets behind its existence. He encounters various adventurers, each with their own unique stories, goals, and abilities. Along the way, Yuuji forms friendships and bonds with these adventurers, and together they face the challenges and dangers lurking in the dungeon.

"Boku no Heya ga Dungeon no Kyuukeijo ni Natteshimatta Ken" combines elements of fantasy, adventure, and slice-of-life as it explores Yuuji's journey from a recluse to a key figure in the dungeon world. The manga offers a mix of light-hearted moments, thrilling encounters, and character growth, as Yuuji embraces his newfound role and the opportunities it brings.

As a long time fan of Windjammers and now Windjammers 2, this scratches the itch for a spiritual successor.

Pros:
Omega Strikers adds a great title to the limited roster of "pickup and play" games with friends.
The "easy to learn, hard to master" gameplay makes it accessible to new players, but there's a depth to appreciate for fans of complex play.
The game strongly encourages going in with a full team, as its fast but manageable pace lends itself well to callouts and team play is crucial for consistent victory. 
The game offers a variety of control schemes so most players will find themselves at home quickly, whether on keyboard or controller. And of course everything is remappable.
If one hero or another doesn’t speak to you, the variety means that you’ll likely find at least a pair that you vibe with. Each hero feels sufficiently unique despite the limited ability set of each. The feeling of each hero can be gleaned in one or two quick play matches, although a testing/training mode would be nice and feels like an obvious oversight. Oh, and new heroes are easily unlocked with free ingame currency you earn by playing any game mode.
Normal matches take a few to get grooving, but the item pick mechanic feels fresh in a dynamic game like this one. Although the roots of the mechanic are obvious: looking at you Richard Henkel, founder of Odyssey Interactive and former lead for Riot’s Teamfight Tactics.

Cons:
The interface and menuing leaves a lot to be desired, and feels like a complete afterthought.
- Hero affinity and session pass XP sometimes does not update until you exit the game and return.
- It's hard to find basic information, such as your level on the ladder (hidden in leaderboard), where to set emotes (in the hero details idk why) or your player profile (in settings).
- Emotes and banners cannot be filtered by what you own, and aren't ordered as such.
- Changing the displayed hero is not intuitive.
But don't worry, the links to their socials are front and center!
It’s a bummer considering the gameplay itself is extremely polished. At least the great art and masterful soundtrack mask the terrible menu design enough to ignore it.
The good news is the devs are active and hard at work, so some of these issues might be resolved by the time you jump in.

TLDR: Good competitive game, really gets your inner gamer going. Highly recommend it if you want something to throw yourself into and feel rewarded for your efforts.

Some games spark that competitive edge inside you and make you want to push further, and I feel that “Omega Strikers” allows that emotion to flourish. I myself have thrown 40 hours into this game and just reached gold, and I don’t even like soccer nor any games similar to it aside from this one.

I feel this was caused by a mixture of things in the game that really get you hooked on the idea of improving and thereby continuing playing the game, those being the “Affinity” system, how rewarding it is to “Git Gud”, and how the game really shows you off once you are “Gud”.

Beginning with the most visible aspect, the “Affinity” system. The more time you dedicate to one character, the more custom things you get for that character. These things range from titles, player cards, poses, and even a sort of “Prestige” striker frame that is displayed when the teams are shown. It really takes the edge off a loss when you internally know you're still progressing towards something, even better those being cool things that show off your dedication towards a character.

As for dedication towards the game, there is a lot you can improve on and once you improve on them you can really feel it be translated into the game. For example, once you get the hang of how to manipulate the ball to where you want to go, you can do some crazy trick shots, which the game actively encourages by making it nigh mandatory to cross up the goalie in order to score. That’s really what I want to get across here, almost every skill feels “good” to improve in. Learning how to predict kicks allows you to steal the ball away from other players and feels “good”, finding out how to position literally makes some goals disgustingly easy and feels “good”. This isn’t even considering mastering your Striker’s abilities, which is a whole entirely different thing to improve on, and you can be sure that once you do so you feel nigh unstoppable. It’s just a game that feels “good” to continue playing.

To elaborate on this “good” feeling, this game constantly celebrates you once you start doing well. The sound of a goal with your character flashing on the screen is way too dopamine inducing, and even gives you a few moments after the goal to really let it sink in that “holy **** I can’t believe I did that.” Knocking out players as well is insanely flashy, looking like something out of “Smash Bros”. Like, seeing an opponent fly across the screen and explode against a wall is soooo good. I don’t know what drugs they infused in this game but it feels designed to induce dopamine while playing it.

Closing thoughts, highly recommend that you grab some friends to start with, screaming in a discord call together is one heck of a fun time. I say that, but the majority of my time was solo cause I'm a [strike]tryharding piece of shi[/strike] competitive. Also, first skill I recommend to “Git Gud” is trying to wait for the opposing team to hit the ball first, then hitting it yourself last. Time it right and they can’t hit it back, letting it fly by them and into their side of the field, or even better, into their goal. Youtube will teach you the rest if you wish to continue to improve. As for characters to start out with, “Julliette” if you want to K.O people, “Dubu” if you want to try goalie, and “Juno” if you want to trip up defenders and get those goals.

Hope to see you climbing the ranks o/

Very unfortunate changes on release date.

Omega Strikers beta was incredible:
- quick 5-10 min matches
- you would preban characters before searching for matches
- you would preselect your "trainings" which would change how your character is played.

Now everything is done during the match.  When I saw how Omega Strikers did it previously i was very happy, and thought "This is a clever way to ban, but not waste everybody's time".

Devs justify new system with limited build variety being played when they specifically forced 2/3 of your build on every character.  Really should've tried removing the restriction and see how the player base worked with the new trainings added.

Instead trainings are now RNG based. After each set you have to pray that nobody picks what you wanted, or be left with a upgrade that doesn't work as well.  A very win-more loop combined with longer game times can feel extremely bad.
Great for a more "fun" game, but sucks on a competitive level.  They also fumbled the bag since the strongest characters on release were boring X, Atlas and Asher.  And the biggest laugh of it, the newest character on release, Zentaro was laughable at best while having a really unique and fun kit.

Matches are now played in a Tennis like matter. Which means it can go on forever.
Previously, if the 5 minutes were up, and there was a difference of 2 points. Good game. Play another.
Now a set can take 5-10 minutes. Theoretically you could play up to 5. (since first to three wins), that's anywhere for 25-50 minutes.
Previously it also felt like as you leveled up, and hit the core harder. That as the match progressed the pacing would increase, speeding up until eventually someone lost. Now pacing restarts constantly with sets.

Additionally it feels like beta players are being screwed over.
- emotes that were rewarded for playing mobile beta previously, are now being given as daily login rewards
- normal currency you could spend on emotes is now useless, since there is a NEW blue currency, for cosmetics.

Even if I would buy all characters i would have 100,000+ credits saved up from beta which mean nothing.

This may be a hot take but I personally feel like the old training systems should be brought back and revamped/balanced and for the awakenings system that is in the game right now be used for a party mode or something else, I felt that matches are to inconsistent for this game to even imagine having a competitive scene with the old training system we had more consistency and to be honest more builds to go on each character I don't believe that the awakenings system was a step in the right direction, as a player who played during the beta I had some of the most fun experimenting with all different types of builds and combos for the characters that were present in the game the idea that I think would be the best way to go about this is to:

+ Make the trainings free for all players so that it is not a grindy experience to unlock them all (this also would remove the argument that training were "pay to win" which was something I commonly heard amongst the OS players that I frequently played and interacted with 

+ Rebalance some of the old trainings in the game for a healthier experience amongst the players of both high elo/low elo play

I believe the the role specific selectable items should stay however as they are the one consistent thing that has been in the games full release so far, and whilst on the subject of the newest additions to the game the spark system is BRILLIANT I adore this system so MUCH this enables you to deal with pesky bruisers by evading or outplaying the enemy with a masterfully placed full spark charge core strike, and whilst I personally despise some of the maps in this game because of how awkward/infuriating the bumper placements are, I feel like the bumper system is a good rewarding challenge that allows for some early game aggressiveness. The time it take to respawn was increased since beta an whilst I can see the reason for the change (being more rewarding to get KO's) I feel like it is way to long to have an advantage over your enemy especially if your goalie is an off pick and whilst I believe in rewarding players for doing well in a match I don't think that getting a lead at the start of the game should dictate how the rest of the match will go. going back to the note of awakenings I genuinely don't think that they are a healthy direction for the game I also don't think that this game should be super early game oriented this give a natural advantage for some characters over others, (this is not me saying that the characters in this game are busted I think that they are pretty well balanced and when a new character comes out of course they are not going to be perfectly balanced) which can make playing this game also feel extremely repetitive just because you see the same characters over and over again and god forbid your character is annoying/meta because you will most likely never be able to play them in ranked.

This feedback comes not from rage or vitriol as this game genuinely holds a place in my heart due to it being the only good game to play amongst the sea of trash whilst it was in beta I wish to see this game grow and it's community alongside with it, however I fear the the barrier to entry will be raised higher than it was in the beta due to confusion around awakenings, and that the player base will start to dwindle due to lack of consistency and mastery over thing that isn't your striker and map that you are playing on.

I will end this feedback with a well done to the developers (if they even ever see this...) for listening to the feedback provided by players and keeping this game healthy and up to date as a low elo player I hope my words are taken into consideration.

A hectic and fast PvP game, you won't find an experience that's as fun and exciting as Omega Strikers on the market, and to help with it all...it's free!

The characters are all really well designed made with great and varied themes as well as personalized songs for each one, fun variety playstyles to try and experiment with, and very well done voice acting. This makes for an attracting and enticing combination that just gets better and better when you actually get into the the game proper.
The gameplay is easy to grasp, its a 3v3 game and the ultimate objective is to swing the bright and shiny yellow puck (Core) into the opposite team's goal. There are plenty of intricacies to figure out in the standard universal mechanics of the game and how each character and each team can function and work together and move all over the map and make choices to accomplish this simple goal, but that is info you'll learn as you play and not something to read up on. Granted, you could watch guides, but personally with this kind of game, nothing beats hands-on experience. 

That experience though does have a few issues currently, and they're ones that the team are more than aware of. 
[strike] A lack of a training mode of sorts or hell, even something that lets you try out characters-purchased or not-in a plain empty arena or square to see how their moves work would benefit players greatly. As much as I am a fan of learning during play, it can help a lot when I know how a move is supposed to work first before I get into the fray. There exists a co-op vs AI mode but I wouldn't exactly call that a training mode.
There's also the lack of a surrender option, which would help make matches with disconnects of any kind less painful to have to play through. This is a point that, if it's keeping you from playing or trying out the game as it is now, I would be understandable since I've dealt with these types of matches already (both when its on my team and on the enemy team) and it's really discouraging. 
Outside of these two obvious cases there aren't things I could complain about Omega Strikers currently. And I would still encourage people to play this game even with those two negatives hanging over it. [/strike]
These issues have been addressed since I've written this review, with the inclusion of an early-leave match ender, a forfeit option within normal and comp matches, and a new practice mode that lets you try everyone.
This should go without saying, but even with these two patches, it doesn't mean the game is issue-free, but how well I know of any are beyond me and needs more active bug reporting from players.

This game is amazing. Its league of legends meets hockey/soccer.

[h1] Overall[/h1]

If you like league of legends you will probably like this. Its less toxic by far and the matches are much shorter. The match starts and you take turns picking your character. Each character has a unique set of abilities and stats. Matches are 3v3. One person on the team will be assigned the Goalie position and the other 2 will be strikers. Then you choose your one item and off you go. Goalies and Strikers have different items to choose from. Each map has a unique "buffer" mechanic that makes it so you have to hit certain spots on the arena to unlock the goal. First to 5 goals wins(In quick play mode or 3 sets of 3 in normals.) if you are playing with real fiends then voice chat is basically a cheat code for this game. The game becomes really exciting and very funny really quickly. We had a blast.


[h1] Pros [/h1]

[list]
 [*]The game isnt pay to win. Its pay for cosmetics. That being said one could potentially spend money and buy all the champions but the game gives you enough free currency that you could buy 2 of the most expensive champs or about 10 of the cheapest ones after only a few hours of playing.
 [*]The game rewards you in several ways with currency and experience towards character mastery which mostly just unlocks more credits to buy more champs or just cosmetics.  
 [*]The gameplay loop is short but very entertaining. It does a very good job of making you feel good when you outskill someone. 
 [*]The visuals are flawless and look amazing
 [*]The game is extremely polished and exhibits zero bugs or issues. 
 [*]There are lots of funny emoji that you can use while in game
 [*]The game does a good job of showing you off when you do good. everyone spectates you when you make a shot. There are nice after shot graphics and unlockable title and image content for your profile. 
[/list]

[h1] Cons [/h1]

[list]
 [*] while the game has around 17 champs at the time of writing this it feels like it needs more. (I read they were going to add quite a bit more before the end of he year)
 [*]The game has a steep learning curve to get great at the game. Killing your opponents is a side project in normals but its life and death here in ranked. 
 [*]Champions need more skins
 [*] champs sometimes feel "too close" to league of legends chracte.

[/list]

This game just isn't for me. I see the potential and the appeal but I just can't follow everything that happens in a match. It feels like if you want to win just pick the characters with the most map pressure. The two new characters have insane moves that either boost their speed alot or cover half the map. It just feels like stimulation overload and their are more matches that feel unwinnable. Maybe I just suck idk. I don't like how much mindgames play into this game as well. The last hit on the core is the only one that matters. Having to wait to hit the core to predict your opponent in a heat of the moment play feels impossible. I also hate how much can happen on the screen at the same time, and when I try to track the core I just completely lose track of where I even am on the map. This game is very overstimulating to me. All of the characters zipping around throwing out countless colorful attacks that launch the core everywhere and are also demolishing your health bar can easily overwhelm you if you aren't used to this type of game. Avoid edges at all cost because purple oni girl will immediately beyblade you into the shadow realm if you're remotely near an edge. It would also be nice if you could hit staggered enemies with just a normal strike because sometimes I would completely stagger an enemy and then have no way to follow up to try to knock them out since my abilities are on cooldown. Then I'm out of position with no pressure and no cooldowns so the enemy team gets to completely ignore me. Some cooldowns feel too long, I feel like if you die and come back you should get all of your cooldowns back. If the enemy team fails to capitalize on a 2v3 or even a 1v3 then they should be punished and the defender(s) should be rewarded with fresh cooldowns. I get that this wants to be a competitive esport with pros in mind but our small simple casual brains are really bad at managing cooldowns so there is a large portion of matches that I feel that I am useless. This isn't a bad game and I know alot of these complaints are personal but I just don't enjoy this one. Don't let my comment discourage you from trying it out yourself. It's worth a shot and I had a few really fun and close games, but the majority of the time I felt like there was nothing I could do. Happy striking. I genuinely hope yall enjoy this one.

Omega Strikers is a really fun air hockey game with a ton of depth. There is already a decent roster size, a handful of maps, and a few modes in place (including ranked with rewards). The game plays like MOBA air hockey, which works very well. The visuals are nice and there are also a lot of free cosmetic unlocks.

The downside of Omega Strikers is the awful character monetization, which hurts players that want to improve or have fun with whoever looks cool (every player). Unlike a competitive game such as Dota 2, you're forced to grind freemium currency to unlock a character or swipe your credit card. The roster, as it stands, is small enough that it's possible to get everyone after about 30 to 40 hours of grinding within a week. Even less time if you take advantage of doing dailies/weeklies and then logging out. That said, this issue will only get worse as the roster size increases. New characters are 50,000 striker credits and your average Normal match (around eight to ten minutes long) will net you 800-1000 credits.

This leads to the next issue with this bad model. If someone is dunking on you with a character and you don't have the credits to unlock them so you can better understand said character, you hit a grind wall where you're out of luck. This model really has no place in a [b]competitive[/b] game and I'm not sure why the developers went with it. You have a "competitive" game where you can't counter-pick or practice bad match-ups through learning characters because you didn't grind enough free currency? Alright, cool, I guess? The game also has a battle pass and a cash shop, so I guess they just threw in this character currency for retention and to make a quick buck off of impatient people.

Despite the character monetization, it's 100% worth playing. I would still highly recommend Omega Strikers. Especially while it's early in its life and you can get everyone quickly.

Game has a lot of potential, but honestly a lot of the decisions are pretty baffling. It went from a fun game that was fairly short in length to one that drags for a long time due to recent changes. This game would have been great as a fun arcadey game but instead the devs are clearly going for an e-sports scene. Huge mistake. E-sports can develop naturally from games that don't even cater or even want them. Trying to push it and actively developing for it is just making the game worse. You can feel this in the recent changes and how the game seems to want to promote that it's "competitive" when in reality it just feels like it's a game that suffers from an identity crisis. 

On one hand the core idea sounds fun, but in practice good players just turn it into a brawl. There are a few characters in the game that basically are incentivized to ignore the soccer portion of the game and treat it like a fighter, X being the most obvious one. You then have the random maps that have some horrendous gimmicks like Atlus' lab that has that exploding gravity well in the middle. Then, to top it all off you have items and levels to further add snowballing to the game as if this were a normal Moba. I like Moba and I enjoy a soccer game here and there... this doesn't fill either niche.

There are things to like about the game like the characters and the fun idea of what it could have been, but I think the game is going to continue to have issues because the devs are full on heading towards the failed e-sport path. Here's a hint to devs, the majority of e-sport titles fail. Most gamers don't care about e-sports and outside of fighting games they only do well in Korea. This isn't a fighting game, even though it feels like it's trying to be, and it isn't a moba. It's a confused soccer game mixed with Smash bros. Genuinely fun concept with a bad execution. I wish it didn't have to be this way, but I'll add this game next to countless others that tried to do e-sports and managed to crash and burn.

This game is truly special. I normally don't do reviews because they usually end up being as long as this one. But I'll review any game that moves me in an extremely positive or negative way.

A few things to preface. I was never much of a League or Dota enjoyer. But I did sink several hundred hours into Smite and Rocket League across Xbox and Steam. I haven't queued for a competitive/ranked match in a game for maybe 2-3 years. This game broke that streak within a couple days and I'm actively having fun every match. Unless I have to go up against aggressive Juno and X forwards. Pain.

The game is incredibly fun with an immense amount of potential, and I'm very confident that the dev team has the competence to hang with the big dogs in the free to play competitive game market. A lot of people keep talking about the Esport potential, and while sure that's here. The most important thing at the end of the day is making a good game that's fun to play.

Pros:
 - Gameplay // It's fun, fast, and the dopamine levels you receive when throwing a well placed, game winning Dubu log nothing can compete.

 - The Dev team // After spending 10 minutes on their subreddit the team is extremely active and engaging with the 
community. They go as far as offering S tier transparency from posters with 3 upvotes, or YouTube videos of people heavily criticizing their game. Explaining the inner working and their thought process of specific changes to the game, and admitting when they've been in the wrong or overlooked something, admitting to their faults. This kind of transparency is rare, especially with how bleak the gaming industry has been recently regarding developer-player relationships.

 - Reward system // The game has a battle pass, yes, it's 2023 and we live in a world where battle passes won't be going anywhere. But this is one of the most fair battle passes I've seen. Of course unless your main is the poster child and has a few sick skins (seems like Rune is the poster child this season with a few recolors of a cool looking skin). They COULD make the battle pass better by offering some premium currency to help repay it back to those actively playing. But I don't mind since they aren't Activision. The team is small and needs funding, not to mention the game already showers you with free stuff all the time. A lot of battle passes snub you with some really lame rewards but you get everything here in the free pass. Emotes, player titles, skins, etc. It's just a matter of if you want to pay $10 for different looking emotes or skins. The striker affinity system is also amazing. The more you play a character, you gain exp for them. Unlocking their own fully free reward track offering special frames, emotes, and poses for that specific character to flex online.

 - Characters // The game has a surprising amount of characters to offer for being so early in its live service cycle, and they all have their own strengths and weaknesses. The cute little nods the strikers have to other characters in their voicelines is also a very nice touch. As of April with an interview with Game Rant they said there is plans on having 26 characters on the roster by the end of the year, they currently have 15 and I'm excited to welcome the new strikers when they come.

 - No text chat // I may be a little in the minority but I think not having text chat for the game is a big bonus. If it does get added in the future please give an option to mute it. (see the semi toxic con below)

Cons:
 - Lack of a practice mode // Of all the criticism of the game this is by far the biggest one I agree with. This was a silly overlook by the team and should have been available the moment players could get their hands on the game. They recently added a co-op vs. ai mode which helps a bit, but they still are lacking the ability to practice characters you haven't purchased yet as a trial run. Let's say little Jimmy wants to step away from Minecraft and try a competitive game because his friends got into it. Little Jimmy is overwhelmed by the amount of characters and just sticks with the default Juliette he played in tutorial. Proceeds to get stomped on in a match because he doesn't know what he's doing and uninstalls the game. 4 years later the game evolves into a powerhouse and hitting 50k concurrent on Steam daily, he'll always remember those matches as Juliette and won't reinstall after his friends beg him to play. Totally not me reflecting my time with League (skull emoji)

 - No leaver penalty // This is another big one I see fairly often and completely agree with that this should have been in the game by now. There's really not much to say about this one besides it just needs to happen, and I hope they add it soon.

 - Ping or quick chat system // The system they already have in place is okay. But could be better. If they adapt more on their quick chat/ping system I strongly believe they won't need a text chat in the game ever. Something akin to Smite I feel will do wonders for their quick chat system. Quick simple button presses that give even more options than before. Such as, pressing down on the D-pad on controller (Keyboard equivalent) opens a menu with: Up=Offensive, Left=Defensive, Right=Special, Down=Back. Selecting one those will open a new menu with options that are more specific to those parent categories. Let's say we select Up=Offensive, our new choices are Up=Pass, Left=KO Them, Right=Spread Out, Down=Burst Ready. Just an idea, but I'd love to see the quick chat system adapted on and improved since I hardly see anyone using it. Plus anything to keep text chat out of the game.

 - Competitive placements // I'm not a personal fan of starting from the very bottom of the ranks and have to crawl up to where you're supposed to be as it just takes a long time if you're better than the average player. Additionally, I feel like this could potentially increase smurfing behavior since the game is free and it's easy to make a new Steam account. But they probably have more data on their end to determine if it will become a real problem or not in the future. 

 - Game modes and balance // I lumped these two together because I was hesitant on including them in the review at all. But figured I'd drop them here as they should be talking points up for discussion or purely informative. The game doesn't have any fun/goofy game modes which after first seeing gameplay I thought some of the maps were the special game modes. The devs have already commented on this and they will have more game modes and activities coming down the pipeline. Including a really sick sounding "cool original mission system with a story-based click-through narrative experience mode" I'm very much looking forward to. Balance is one thing that will be up for debate as the game ages. They've stated they plan on doing weekly balance changes but I fear that this isn't enough time for the players to find a meta and for the dev team to crack down on it. I agree with them that a monthly balance schedule is too long, especially in the birth of the game, but maybe bi-weekly balance changes would allow them more time to focus development time on other aspects of the game rather than worrying if X is still too busted.

In conclusion: I'm genuinely excited to watch this game grow in the future and I'll continue to play and support because they have something very good going for them. There aren't many games that give me a good feeling for their future of if they will succeed in the long run. But this is easily one of them that has a bright future.

I can safely say here, at its current state, it's honestly a fantastic little game you can sink an hour or two a day or even just play on the go. Would it ever replace a proper MOBA? Definitely not, but the game itself feels far better to just pick up and play without learning too much at all. Quickplay is perfect for just getting a few games in and feels fine to just play. Normal and ranked are definitely the meat and potatoes when it comes to comps and picking awakenings, and the overall gameplay just feels slick and rewarding, although it is very ping reliant.

As for negatives? Well it's designed to be as inclusive of a game as possible, so if things feel like they're mobile game-ish, you're not far off from that assumption, since it is a mobile title too. UI is definitely a fickle, it's very all over the place. It's missing things like a stat tracker, so things like goals landed, saved shots, total KOs, W/L, etc is currently not available, and there's no penalty system for leavers/griefers/afkers etc, but they are addressing those already as time goes on. The game did suffer the state of we need this game as polished as possible before releasing with the sacrifices to the UI and UX, but it's more or less in a state where it's quick enough for the main things.

Give it a shot if you're looking for something that fills the niche of what Battlerite did. It's actually pretty banger.

I know what the game looks like at first glance but surprisingly enough, there is quite a bit of enjoyment that can be gained through playing Omega Strikers. It's a fun football (or "soccer") take on the classic MOBA gameplay genre which is majorly improved with the inclusion of allowing friends on your team.
There are (as of writing this) fifteen strikers to choose from, four of which being available from the get-go and each having cool, unique designs, exhilarating styles of gameplay and even backstories that never make one individual feel like the sole main character this whole world revolves around. Unrelated but my personal favourite is fellow dapper Brit: Rasmus.
Speaking of characters, however, let's get into the flaws; many of them are pretty unfair to go against, especially when they're in specific roles on the field. Many balance updates are definitely required before we reach a satisfying neutral ground of being able to deal with each opposing character. It also feels a bit too easy to be considered an "expert" at a striker, gaining this title upon reaching Level 5 on any one of their affinities but this is more-so a nitpick on my part.
Another thing is the fact that you can only have 3 people in a party as that's the limit per team. This is understandable for balancing reasons but unfortunate for those wanting to get a few more friends in with you. Custom games do exist though, so that's certainly a slight fix for this single unfortunate necessity.
Overall though, Omega Strikers has certainly exceeded my expectations since being shown its store page by a friend. A lot of fun, would one-hundred percent recommend.

I would give this game an overwhelmingly positive review if possible, and that's even though I have some issues with the game as well. I'm writing this after the game's first micro patch announcement where they talk about what they want to fix as well, so here's the good and bad.

*GOOD*
The game is free, so try it, it's VERY fun. It's very likely my favorite competitive free-to-game that I've played in years, and it's REAL addictive. Matches are short (sometimes very short), and even playing a best of 5 in Normal or Competitive comes and goes within about 10 minutes. The controls take a little bit of time to learn based on who you're playing, but you can pick this up incredibly fast as most abilities are straight-forward. The online community in-game is fairly kind, with lots of thumbs up and pogs when you score, and I've even seen the other team cheer us on during the closer games. The art style is incredibly cohesive and has a solid identity and vibe, and the opening animation by Trigger really sells the feel of this game and the personality of the characters. Finally, the devs seem cool! During the first announcement for what they plan to fix, I kept saying "THANK YOU" to every talking point, meaning they have been incredibly proactive so far in listening to the community and are doing what they can to make this game good, and seem to have ears on the ground for what changes to make. I'm more used to the free-to-play market being more focused on in-game transaction pushes rather than community feedback, so this is really nice. In terms of in-game purchases, I'm weak and spent $20 on some cute skins, but I don't feel like it's pushed at all. I love that I'm unlocking other characters by just playing the game a lot, and I'm able to unlock a new character every couple of days of playing or so, which means I don't see myself ever needing to pay to play the whole roster if I didn't wanted to. Also, the cosmetics are very cute, which goes back to how banger the art team is with this game. I wanna see this game grow a lot, and I'm shocked there's been no fanart of these character yet, and really wanna see a small community grow here.

*BAD*
On the smaller level of bad, I'm still a little lost on some of the game's terminology. They actually have an in-game glossary of the game's lingo and mechanics, and while that's great it still leaves out a lot of terms. For example, I have zero idea what Spark is or what it does. I looked in the glossary, thought I paid attention in the tutorial, and while I could google what it means maybe, I shouldn't have to and things like that should really be explained better. The lack of a practice/training mode makes this harder, because it means you sorta need to throw a game or two in order to learn how a new character works, which isn't fun for your teammates. Finally, the worst part of the game: AFK and players dropping from games. It happens a strange amount, and even in Overwatch or Fortnite I never see the amount of AFK instances like I see in this game. You can't do anything about it either, if your teammate stops moving or leaves entirely, you're forced to play that best of 5 anyways knowing you're going to lose. There isn't a penalty or ban for dropping like this either. And, on the off chance you have that dog in you and decide you wanna quit too because a teammate dropped, you can't just close out the game and reboot it because surprise: when you restart the game, it will open and force you back into that same game, meaning you have to wait to play again until it's over. While I wouldn't recommend ever DQing from any online team game, the fact of the matter is that this is the game at it's least fun. Just today it happened so often that I just played a different game because I was sick of losing rank in competitive just because a teammate decided to dip. 

Luckily, the devs have addressed the lack of a practice mode, AFK, and drop outs in the micro patch update, and are at least working on it. They even said they are planning to add a forfeit feature, which is ABSOLUTELY needed, although I hope you don't lose rank for forfeiting if you're doing it because you're down a player. If anything, while it's irritating, I almost wish the game would just automatically call the match a draw when there's a player down, but that's just me. I severely hope they can fix this issue because this problem is almost frequent and bad enough that it almost ruins the entire experience of the game, which isn't fair because 90% of the time otherwise it's fantastic. Overall, the game is absolutely worth picking up and trying, and if the devs manage to give penalties or bans to the players who are making the game a bad experience, I think this game has amazing potential, and is still fun all the same.
