Really fun game both for casual play and competitive players.

The core (pun intended) is very simple. Just hit the ball (core) back and forth until you get a goal. Every hero has the same strike ability to do this with. This on its own would already be pretty fun and replayable honestly.
On top of that core gameplay all the different heroes have some extra abilities to help getting the core (and enemy players) where they want. There are a lot of different playstyles from characters who excel at beating other players up to characters that excel at influencing the core from longer range.

They also added awakenings, which give every normal or competitive game some more variety which really helps to keep the game more replayable. Games are a best of 5 series where each of the 5 sets are first to 3 points. After each set the players draft an awakening (a buff in some unique way). This makes it so some games your ultimate ability is really strong, other games one or more of your basic abilities have stronger qualities and some other games your base stats (speed, health, power) are more solid. This gives the game a bit of a roguelite feel that I never expected in a MOBA-style game.

There is a really fun learning curve. Once you get to higher ranks or play with friends you start seeing more passing to teammates instead of just hitting the ball straight back where it came from or always directly towards the enemy goal (barriers).

The only problems I've found in this game are with people going AFK and that some people get salty and BM with emotes a bit, but I don't think that can be helped in any team-based competitive-like game. 
It really helps that you only have 3 people per team to reduce the chance of having someone negatively impact your games. That also makes it a lot easier to have a fully premade team.

Omega Strikers is the best F2P game I've played. It's really fast-paced, fun and pretty generous when it comes to the currency with which to unlock strikers (read heroes/champs). Even though it still has some issues, that I'm confident they'll address, and even though I get salty if I get bad teammates I would highly recommend anyone give this a try. I hope this game has a bright future ahead of it.

But even with those limitations, it's still very fun!

The worst parts are players that go AFK/leave intentionally, or those that disconnect due to internet issues. As well as the occasional try hard or someone that is a bit toxic with the emote spam and blame game. Ignore them, start another round, and find those nice, good, friendly players out there, because there are plenty. 

Overall a great game! Especially for being 100% free, only paying for cosmetics or to optionally unlock things quicker. Plenty of interesting characters to choose from with awesome and fairly unique game play!

EDIT: My friend and I got a 15 minute ban because we were "AFK" during a griefing match where the opponents refused to score on us. We were already punished having to sit through a 21 minute match where we CAN'T FORFEIT, and WOULD be punished for leaving early, and now we're ACTUALLY punished for standing around and refusing to face 3 players playing keep away while our goalie was disconnected.

This game is still good, but the systems in place are TERRIBLE as of right now. There is no way to end a game with trolls other than being punished yourself, and they decided to install punishments BEFORE adding forfeit options... Just a horrible design choice.
Review will remain negative until this is ever solved.

EDIT 2: They finally added forfeits... and it was done so horrendously.
-First of all the option is not available DURING a set, meaning the same problem my friend and I faced still exists and blights can still get away with their griefing.
-Even between sets, the option is not always given. It only shows up IF the game detects a missing teammate, or if you LOSE 2/3 rounds. Meaning you're stuck in games you don't want to be in still, and can't choose to forfeit if you're winning too easily.
-And even when the option is there, it does not give any indication of a teammate wanting to forfeit. It should ALWAYS be visible, and should have a sound play when a teammate votes so you don't need to guess and check.
-If you do vote, you need the ENTIRE team to vote yes, or the game continues. No majority of votes, it must be unanimous, so 1 player can ruin it for 2 others.
-Lastly the update added an automatic match ending system if they detect someone leaves, taking the option out of the hand of the players. So goodbye to awesome rounds of 2V3 where you WANT to stay and continue playing, which is where I met some of my best teammates before.

All in all this shows they are at least trying to fix things, but this is still a TERRIBLE system that supports negative gameplay and harms those who want to have a good time. Review is remaining negative until this is changed.

EDIT 3: The devs are abandoning this game before it has even been out for a single year, claiming they can't grow it. Meanwhile they ignore the tons of comments and request from the player base and do nothing to improve the experience for new players to understand the game.

Y'know, I genuinely want to like this game. it takes mechanics from games that I love playing (League of Legends, Rocket League) and combines them into one but this game is absolutely ruined by a litany of issues.

Before I get into this, I'm in no way claiming to be a god at this game, and understand I have lots of room to improve. With that being said:

Firstly, there is zero, I repeat, ZERO, repercussions for leaving the game. I have had countless leavers, and what does the game do to reprimand leavers or aid shorthanded teams? literally nothing. If its Quick Play, I couldn't care less. But Ranked? When playing in a 3 stack with some friends and down heavily, we tested this theory. my buddy left the game, waited for it to finish, and received ZERO matchmaking penalty or even MMR loss.

Now let's get into the map issue. The arcade map is just absolutely atrocious. Visually pleasing? Yes. Playable? No. The map only has one paddle to break before the net opens when other maps have two making the rallies extremely short. The paddle is also away from the wall making it incredibly easy to hit by guiding the core along the corner, that is unless the goalie in question is Dubu or Atlas. Dubu is so massive from game start without any awakenings that he can literally just sit on top of the paddle and hit it from any side, and Atlas can spawn his giant omnipotent core blocker right on top of it. Rasmus also turns from a mediocre character to an absolute S+ tier demon on this map because the center has a hole that acts as an out of bounds and he will just stand behind it the whole game and hook you in, where you will die regardless of your HP.

There is also a severe lack of communications options. With the only way to talk to your teammates being pinging, seemingly everyone takes pings as BM. No i'm not trying to hurt your precious ego, I just genuinely think its a good idea if we spread out. At least give us some Playskool team chat where we can't say the big boy words. Are companies these days really that afraid of their games being toxic that I can't communicate at all? MAKE A CHAT THAT'S OPTIONAL.

But none of this compares to the single largest issue of the game. Bruisers. They barely get knocked back, stun lock your goalie, and just make the game unplayable. They literally don't even attempt to hit the ball. Its genuinely infuriating when you can't even move let alone outplay. I got to about High Silver (Top 5000 NA, Top 14K Global, all Flex queued) and the game devolves to just fighting. its not fun at all when you spend so much time learning to play the game one way just for it to be tossed out the window completely. On top of that, in ranked your entire team only gets one ban so unless your get lucky or play in a 3 stack you only have a 33% chance of banning the striker you select. And let's not forget your random teammates banning the character you were about to play. The most notable character that makes you wanna commit scooter ankle are X, Asher, and Zentaro. Down below I will go in depth with each character.

X, the most common of the screw-playing-the-game strikers that people select is easily the most annoying. His ult allows his ball strikes to hit enemies and he will just walk up to your goalie and start punching. He feels like he never gets knocked back, and he has an AoE stun as well. Oh yea, and his dash stuns as well so that means that ALL of his abilities have CC. The cherry on top is the unfathomable knockback he does, which when you are goalie is more than enough to knock you into the net and out of the game while you are just stuck perma CC'd. And so many awakenings aid him in doing so. Special cooldown, Primary or secondary charges, Stagger buffs, impact buffs, doesn't matter, they just make him scale out of control so there isn't much room for comeback. He's also so easy to play, I believe Koko the gorilla could be Omega rank with him.

If you get lucky enough to ban X, you get Asher. Asher has a shield that if you play goalie and when placed close to you makes it practically impossible to clear the core. On top of that her hit box is so massive that she can easily counter your strikes and any size increase from awakenings spells game over for you.

Zentaro has a point and click easy attacking move that takes up massive space and shoots the ball in a random location. Unhittable while doing so. His whole kit is built to attack you and is easily just as good at elimating your goalie as X but instead of stun locking you he's untargetable.

Atlas also has a shield similar to Asher but he also has an AoE move he just drops infront of his net making it unscorable, or right in front of your face you you walk into it and lose 3/4 of your HP. He also just has an ult that makes his teammates unkillable so he'll just pop that the second any of his low HP teammates are in danger.


All I can say is, its a shame that a game that has the potential to be so fun can get so clouded with people just playing like its Super Smash Bros. instead of a coordinated team effort and no way to even talk to my team and strategize. But I can't even blame the player base, it's the devs who gave these monkeys the tools to do so and kickstarted their stone age.

And initially, I liked it! It was fun! I even recommended it to my friends and thought it'd be a laugh. But then the cracks started to show...

The gameplay is... It's not exact, let's put it that way. Many, many times, both me and my friends said, 'how did that not hit?' or, 'I swear that was next to me' and yet, the 'core' (I call it the ball, but it has a different name) will sometimes just breeze through you. The balance is all over the place.

But the biggest, most egregious, error with this game is that this is a TEAM game. It is made for 3 people to play against 3 other people. That is the game, yes? We're agreed on that, right? Then why the f*** have the developers made it so damn hard to communicate with your fellow players?! 

Want to coordinate to cross the core and score? Good luck! All you have are emotes based around Internet memes. Want to tell the goalie to get back because they're over-extending? Good luck! All you have is a Pepe emote. Want to ask the forward to help you out because you've got your Q and you know you can hit it down the right hand side? You have 'Help!' as an emoji, and that's it.

Look, I get it. MOBA's have a history of being toxic. That's true. I understand. But Omega Strikers has taken that concern and ramped it up to its maximum level. You might as well not even have emotes; they're absolutely useless.

I mean, asides all that, it has a battle pass and apparently the game had a way better system before, so this game seems to be getting worse as it goes on. But if you join the official Discord, like I did, you'll just see a heap of people thinking this is the best game ever, so don't expect anything to improve soon.

All in all, it's a shame this game is so bad. It could be cool, it really could. It could even be a household name like Apex or Rocket League, but it won't, because the devs want to be down with the kids rather than making a properly functioning game.

Just writing a review to support all-mighty algorithm-based lords, since I genuinely think the game deserves it, and I have no clue how to write reviews for "online only strictly multiplayer based games." Before anything else though, my experience with the game is entirely based on playing with friends, so I have no clue what the experience is like playing with random people.

Getting that out of the way, Omega Strikers is a very "what you see is what you get type of game", which is to say, there are no sneaky or dubious design decisions lurking and buried deep inside the game that will disappoint you a couple of hours in, so if from the get-go the game seems right up your alley, it is highly encouraged to give it a try. 

Whether you come from Rocket League, MOBAs, hero based shooters, or what have you, Omega Strikers genuinely offers an experience with a low enough skill floor for anyone to pick up and play, but a high enough ceiling that makes you keep coming back for more. This makes it so that in each match there is a perfect balance of chaotic energy mixed with skill-based gameplay, where you start contributing just by kicking the ball forward, but will end up later down the line executing some sweet combos to secure a victory.

Characters are diverse, playing in a varied way and matching up differently with each other, and overall the character design on a visual level is also quite solid. Interesting visual identity is mostly reserved to the characters though, as everything else can be described by being serviceable, aka doing its job. The music can also be a bit bland and brain dead, but otherwise in terms of overall sound and sfx there is quite a hefty work behind it and everything sounds beefy. For those that don't know what "story" is anymore, and only understand the concept of "lore", the game delivers the obligatory quota in order to give everything a bit of context, but not much else.

The truth is, the core game displayed here is overwhelmingly solid, basically carrying everything else since there are no other elements bogging it down. No pay to win shenanigans since the premium currency is exclusively used for cosmetic stuff, no overwhelming "time-limited" progression where one can miss important features by not playing during one single day, etc... The game gets a lot of love from the development team, there is no egregious matchmaking or networking, the gameplay is polished, what else could you want? It's a bit sad that when it comes to games with this format, one must explicitly state everything that is NOT wrong, but I guess in this case it sort of works as the game's biggest compliment. In a perfect world one should be able to say "gameplay good = game good, enough said", but in this case, that literally is what happens with Omega Strikers. If you want solid, distinct, polished, fun, team based gameplay, then you will probably like this game.

TLDR, the game has Studio Trigger's blessing, get it now

Omega Strikes? More like Air-hockey on crack. 

So, OS is a 3v3 quasi-sports game, where you and your teammates are tying to get the ball in the opposing sides goal, often by first removing some sort of protective barrier. To assist you in this task, each character comes equipped with 3 abilities with a MOBA feeling to them. The first team to score 5 points win. 

Now, this game is very very fast and things can swing on a dime if your not paying attention, and it can be deeply frustrating to see a game turn from a sure win to a painful loss, but at the same time very satisfying for the opposite to happen. I find the presentation to be charming, funny and i enjoy the character design, both in artistic and a gameplay sense. There is a ton of memes, references and nerd stuff in the game as well, and while i find it cute/funny, i am sure it would be a turn-off for some people. 

Is the game generous with its content? Not sure, but after the tutorial, i could already acquire 4 more strikers (the cheaper ones) to my line-up, giving me 7 in total. I hope the game adds a try-out or testing system, so you can see what sorta play-style a Striker has before you buy it. Cosmetics, nameplates and all that jazz is here as well, but is of very little interest to myself. 

Now bad things: As mentioned, this game can be very frustrating in the same way a Fighting game can be frustrating. If you are playing with randoms, you can get supremely unlucky and lose a match even if you did everything right. I am assured that there toxicity somewhere, just like in all these MOBA-adjacent games, but with no chat its hard to see it. Also, since you can't test Strikers, and their gameplay overviews are not always super clear, you might wanna watch a clip or two on youtube first before you buy one, so that you know what you are getting. 

Overall, i see this as a solid 6 or 7 out of 10 sort of game. Its fun, its fast and its the kind of game you can play one or two matches of and then move on to something ells, and i am sure that with a good friend or two, it can become a great experience. I hope it sticks around and gets a solid playerbase, for the developers have put in some great work in this game.

In a lot of competitive online games there's some form of downtime, like looting in a battle royale for example, (even if it isn't necessarily fun) that takes a bit of the mental load off for a bit. The quick play matches on the other hand were a bit too short and in a good number of them I would either be steamrolled or (as I played the game more) steamroll the other team. I'd like to see a mode in between competitive and quick play, maybe a First to Two rounds, with a score of 3 or maybe 5 per round, with everyone drafting an item before the first round so you have more time to have fun with that system but the matches don't take as long. Finding a cool and unique game that is actually fun these days is rare, so seeing one kill itself right before my eyes is incredibly disappointing.

The game in its beta state felt complete and was incredibly fun. Matches were fast paced and whichever team achieved five points, by a margin of two, won the match. Now, outside of quickplay, both teams have to reach three sets of three points with a pause in between sets for everyone to pick what were once trainings one could choose before a match. These are passive boosts to an aspect of a character that can help them reach their full potential, and are now erased after the match has ended. They are also random, which means you may not be able to play your character in your specific playstyle for what are now higher-stakes 20-30 minute matches. The magic of the previous version was how quickly you won if you were more skilled than your opponents, how quickly you lost if they were more skilled than you, and how tense matches got if both teams were equally skilled trying to get two points above the other. Losses didn't matter since you could easily get into another match afterwards, and getting on a win streak felt all the more satisfying. You could play hours of matches and not realise how much time has passed. Now matches are long enough to have one or two be exhausting.

The developer's justification of the temporary, randomised trainings mid-match is that the longer the beta was live, the more similar each match felt. This was a good thing, as it allowed the players to become accustomed to their characters and how they were supposed to function given the right trainings for the player's playstyle. Now it is easy to forget which ones you chose in the 15 seconds your are given to chose when you consider how chaotic the actual gameplay is. Additionally, Counter-Strike hasn't changed in twenty years, and it seems to be doing well for itself. Having matches be similar is not a fault, but the current system
they made to combat a non-issue is.

Another thing that makes matches take too long is the addition of what I will call goal-blocks. Previously, there were walls that retracted and extended throughout the match that blocked both goals. Whichever team was in the lead had their walls retract faster than the team losing, giving the team losing a chance to attack for a short time while their wall was still extended. Whoever is in the lead doesn't need an advantage over the other team, so the design at the time was good. Now there are goal-blocks. These are difficult to hit targets near each team's goals that will retract the walls once all are hit with the ball. This makes matches drag on, as one goalie can usually guard at least one of the goal-blocks for a long time, which means even more time spent in a game that used to have quick and fun matches. The charm of the worldwide beloved sport of football/soccer is that there's one person guarding a large goal with the help of the other players that are outside of the goal box, so adding a mechanic that makes it impossible to score unless you hit a prerequisite makes the game not fun.

Everything else that has changed is at most a minor annoyance, such as splitting up the end-game screen into three screens, so it's more difficult to share a screenshot of if you had a good game.

A common "gotcha" to the changes in ranked and the normal gamemodes include "Just play quickplay so you don't have to deal with the changes." What if you want to play the game you once loved with people around your skill level? Quickplay does not take skill level into account when forming players for a match, only ping. This means that the probability of completely destroying or being destroyed by the other team increases, and while it's nice for an ego boost, it's preferable to play opponents around your skill level to challenge yourself; Something you can no longer do if you prefer the previous version's gameplay compared the the current.

I will gladly change this review if these issues are fixed. It baffles me how a team can make a game for years, show off a fantastic pre-release product, and kill it in front of you when it was supposed to be finished.

Underwhelming Experience: Omega Strikers Falls Flat

I'm still trying to figure out why I wasted my time on Omega Strikers, a free game that was heavily promoted by content creators. As someone who's always eager to try out new games, I was thoroughly disappointed by this shallow, mundane, and tacky experience.

From the moment I started playing, I knew something was off. The graphics were subpar, the sound effects were annoying, and the gameplay was repetitive and unengaging. But what really got my blood boiling was the fact that this game was pushed by popular content creators, who seemed more interested in raking in the views and ad revenue than providing an honest review of the game.

It's clear that these creators were only in it for the clicks and the ad money, and their fake enthusiasm and over-the-top praise for Omega Strikers only served to further disappoint me. I mean, who are they kidding? This game is a mess, and it's not even worth the time it takes to download it.

The gameplay itself is a snooze fest. The objective is to score goals, but the mechanics are so simplistic and unoriginal that it feels like I'm playing a watered-down version of a real sports game. The characters are bland and uninteresting, with no depth or backstory to speak of.

Overall, I would not recommend Omega Strikers to anyone. It's a free game, but it's still a waste of time. If you're looking for a real gaming experience, look elsewhere.

This game has an unfortunate issue with leavers,  which the beta did not have. Personally I think some of the changes made heavily incentive's leaving a match.

The main changes that I think contribute the issue are game length, the new goal opening mechanics, and an influx of players that through no real fault of their own have no idea what they are doing.

During the beta, if you were a part of a team with a player that was an active detriment, the game would end quickly and you would spend maybe 4 minutes max in that frustrating situation. Same would go for if you had someone disconnect or leave. The other team would have little difficulty scoring and even if you somehow managed to hold out, the timer would run down and you would naturally lose.

Now during the beta, if you have a teammate that is an active detriment or has left, it can take up anywhere from 10-15 minutes to lose a game. The objectives to open up the goal are much easier to defend, which means that it takes longer for the team with the advantage to score, and makes it practically impossible for the disadvantaged team to sneak a goal in.

Not only that, but even if you are down 2 sets to 0, the other team being 6 goals ahead, you still have to sit through a power picking phase and three more goals. The goals which are artificially lengthened due to having to open them up.

Currently there are three options when faced with this type of situation. 
1. Leave the game
2. Play your best
3. Give up and let the other team score

Leaving the game is selfishly the most desirable option, since it immediately allows you to leave a situation that isn't fun and allows you to do something more enjoyable. But since there isn't an official surrender/leave the game option that isn't punished, this isn't really an option and is instead the problem.

Obviously the option that everyone including the devs would probably prefer is for everyone in the game to keep playing their best. But with the game mechanics that delay the game outlined before, this means you could spend an extra 15 minutes in a game that you have no chance of winning. Even worse, a game that just isn't fun.

Lastly is to just give up and let the other team score. This option isn't punished but is basically the same as leaving the game except that you still have to sit there for around 4 minutes waiting for the other team to win.

If all of this was just an outlier it would be fine, but in the last 4 games (only 4 since release) I have played I have seen someone on a team leave the game. In one game it took our team 10 minutes to win a 3v2. It was not a close game, they never even opened up our goal, but our strikers still struggled to get past a dubu defending the small bar that would open THEIR goal. In another game, both of my teammates left halfway through the second set and I still had to sit through 5 goals and a power picking phase.

I played for over 60 hours during the beta and eagerly awaited the return of the game for the last few months. But now that it's here, I still have not had a game that I actually enjoyed.

[h2]Update[/h2]
They have announced that they are no longer updating this game. It is abandonware after being out for a year

[h2]Summary[/h2]
Feels like a fan game for some unknown anime. Great as amateur work, not as professionals.

[h2]The Good[/h2]
- Graphics are nice
- Heaven for weebs

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
- Cash grab
- Awful UI/UX
- Cringe fest: overuse of memes, too much streamer content, stats for the sake of stats

[h2]Details[/h2]
This really could be a pretty fun, decent game. But the overall experience was simply just frustration for my friends and I.
The issues I list below, combined with the emphasis on the cash shop and season pass, doesn't make me feel like this game was made with love or care. It feels more like a cash grab.

[b]Janky UI/UX[/b]
They need to hire a better UI/UX designer. The menus are non intuitive, you have no idea where anything is unless you randomly start clicking around, If you go to the store to buy a character, you can't see their details at all. You have to exit the store and check the characters from the character list to see their information.

[b]Stats/Terminology[/b]
This game seems to suffer from stats for the sake of stats. Nothing really seems to really mean anything. A character's overview page has added bonus stats without any explanation of why.

Example
Damage: 250 =  200+100%
Why is there a +100% to the damage? Why does a base damage have bonus damage?

A useful stat like the health pool of your character though? non-existant. Moves will state something like "35% increase speed" but you have no idea what that really means since you don't even know your character's base speed anyways. To describe each move, there's a lot of "flavor text", but no useful information. Again, nothing like the range of a move or area of effect.

[b]Memes[/b]
From voice lines to text, they try to fill it with memes and jokes as if to say "we too are like you guys, we're gamers!"

[b]Streamer Content[/b]
Clearly, this game launched as a partnership to many streamers or they have paid many streamers to work along side them. For someone who doesn't care, it's very overwhelming. Streamer icons, streamer emotes, streamer backgrounds, it's pushed far too much.

The game is free to play, and not pay to win.

To preface, I played Omega Strikers when it was first released in its early access phase and very much enjoyed the game. While much of what made it fun has been carried over to the latest version of the game is still there, there are some changes which have made it significantly less enjoyable for me. Primarily, the introduction of the Awakening system has bogged down a skill-intensive game with a ton of rng and severely crippled its balance. The novelty of drafting power ups between rounds quickly loses its luster when you have to deal with an unstoppable build after just one round. And this brings me to my next complaint: game length.

What was great about the early release was how quick matches were with my sole complaint being that they would sometimes get repetitive on account of the relatively small character and map variety. They've somewhat remedied the map situation as obstacles play a more substantial role in the new maps (which isn't always for the best), and the introduction of a couple of new characters has fleshed out the roster more. However, the additions of new maps and the Awakening draft system has dragged out match times to excruciating lengths, which is only made worse by the fact that the initial power-ups selected by players often determine the outcome of the match. So, having to sit through a game for another fifteen minutes becomes incredibly tedious at that point. Regardless of whether I'm winning or losing, the key appeal for me of quick, competitive games is completely lost now.

I still think Omega Strikers is fun, and it absolutely has promise, but it's not a game that can be taken remotely seriously--as far as competitive play goes--in its current state. The team has positioned themselves in a place where serious balance issues and a radical overhaul of the game's systems have introduced major problems that were not present with the earlier version. I'm hopeful that it's not a matter of IF they'll address these issues but rather WHEN they will.

I like to think of this game as a hyper-condensed MOBA. The map is small enough to fit on one screen and the action is incredibly fast-paced, and this fixes many of the issues many MOBA's have. Probably the best thing to come from this is the ability to see your teammates at all times. You can much better coordinate shots, spot mistakes from your teammates, and even understand when you are the one who isn't pulling their weight, and adjust accordingly. I remember one game I played our goalie was having a rough time. I offered to defend for him, and he went on a scoring streak while I kept the goal much safer, nearly allowing us to win a match we were very behind in. There is one massive issue, however, that carries over from the MOBA genre, and it's especially bad here: leavers. There is no way to leave a match from the pause menu, but that doesn't stop players from closing the application and leaving that way. This wouldn't be too much of a problem, except that there is no way to end a match early. And at that point you are at the mercy of the opponents, who can make that game as short or, more terrifyingly, as long as they want to. Adding a "vote forfeit" that the whole team has to agree to would go a long way towards helping this issue. I hate to make this review mostly focused on a single bad thing, but it is a big issue with a simple fix. I have basically no other qualms about the game and would highly recommend it to others.

Ingredients

    1 tbsp vegetable oil
    8 skinless boneless chicken thighs
    8 rashers smoked streaky bacon, cut into large pieces
    1 onion, halved and sliced

    200ml milk

    1 egg, beaten

Method

    STEP 1

    Heat the oil in a large, non-stick frying pan. Season the chicken thighs and fry for 5-8 mins until golden brown, turning occasionally. You may need to do this in two batches, depending on the size of your pan.
    STEP 2

    Lift the chicken onto a plate and tip the bacon pieces into the pan. Fry for 5 mins until crisp. Add the onion, mushrooms and thyme sprigs, then fry on a high heat for another 3 mins until the onions start to colour. Tip the flour into the pan and cook, stirring, for 1 min.
    STEP 3

    With the pan off the heat, gradually stir or whisk in the chicken stock, followed by the milk, then add the chicken back to the pan.
    STEP 4

    Bring to the boil, then simmer for 30 mins. Spoon the filling into a large pie or baking dish (approx 20 x 30cm) with a lip and leave to cool.
    STEP 5

    Heat the oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7. On a floured surface, roll the pastry to the thickness of two £1 coins. Cut a long strip as wide as the rim of the pie dish and, using a little of the beaten egg, fix to the edge of the pie dish. Brush with beaten egg, then lift the rest of the pastry over the pie, using the rolling pin to help. Gently press the edges with your fingers and trim with a sharp knife.

Genuinely, this may be the best game I'll ever have the pleasure of playing. I'm not sure how Odyssey created a MOBA air hockey game that feels like a fighting game at times, but they did, and it is a truly unique experience. Jumping into Omega Strikers is refreshing in a way. So many games nowadays has one or two different comparisons to it, genre bloaters if you will. Omega Strikers, though, the very best way I could describe it is Super Rocket League of Legends Bros..

Try this game out, you have only to gain.

I'm not a fan of sports games, to be honest, the only category i overall like less than sport is first person shooters. I do play some MOBA games once in a while, played for some thousands of hours on LOL in the past (retired) and some 100 hours on pokemon unite and HOTS.

With that said, this is an air hockey MOBA, there is the quick back and forth action of trying to get the puck into the opponents' goal, but there is also just kicking the opponent off the arena so they are out for a few seconds.

If this was FIFA, i'd not even give it a chance, I've seen gameplay of traditional sports games and while i can watch them, every time i've tried them myself, even if i win, i'm still not having fun. Now THIS game, i can lose and still have fun! just the quick back and forth as a forward, or teleporting with AI.ME across the map to score that perfect goal, to the great feeling when you get a good teamplay going! All of it is just fun and entertaining, it's having me lean forward so much in my seat it's a miracle i've not fell on the floor yet!

So now that i've praised the game, there are a few gripes i have with the game outside of the gameplay itself, the menus are kind of confusing to navigate, the resolution is locked to 1080p (or less) unless you run exclusive fullscreen, I really don't like playing games in exclusive fullscreen. Even if 1080p looks fine, i still want the option to run native. in-game the mouse and keybaord controls feels a little stiff compared to controller, but it might just be a me problem. It takes pretty long to get coins to buy new characters, granted, it's usually the same in most MOBAs, and this game is plenty fun so i don't really mind it that much.

In conclusion, I recommend this game for anyone that likes MOBAs or just generally like fast-paced air hockey.

[h1] Omega Strikers Short Review[/h1]
As of May 1, 2023,

Omega Strikers is a fun game plagued by the same problem that popular Free-to-play titles suffer from AFK players and Trolling. In those games, strict measures ensure that the behavior is less frequent, but regrettably, Omega Strikers doesn't feature anything like that. The abandonment runs so deep in this game that players leave competitive matches when the enemy team scores on average. It happens way too much and then the player is stuck in a 2 VS 3 which is unwinnable 90% of the time.

In addition, some characters seem to be too valuable for their good. For example, AI MI makes Estelle useless; they feature near identical kits of abilities with the difference that AI MI can put down a turret that has no counterplay if use correctly. The turret will keep hitting the disk constantly; no matter how much you try to take it out, it will remain locked in your court. She is a better version of Estelle in every sense.

Until more brutal punishments are delivered to AFK players, and some re-balancing is done to the characters, I recommend passing up on this game. The current state of Omega Strikers feels like an Alpha and its brilliant art direction and character designs are the only excellent redeeming quality it has to offer.

5/10 MEDIOCRE.

It's hard to give this game a negative review, cause I actually keep playing and enjoy this game - but here are the MAJOR issues it has (and if you can TOLERATE these issues, you will have a blast, cause the game is fun):

1. There is literally no way to coordinate the team. There is no chat, there is only a PING system. The issue with it is that it doesn't contain the most IMPORTANT information: "We have a Goalie, STOP STANDING RIGHT NEXT TO HIM" and "Spread out and pass the ball around - don't both run at the same spot". 

When you play with people, that is the most COMMON MISTAKE people make. They either hug the Goalie all the time, which makes his job harder (there is nobody to pass the ball to, and it's hard to tell where your teammate will kick the ball). And you cannot tell them in any way to NOT DO THAT. "Spread out" and "Let me Defend" just don't convey "Go ATTACK" and "Don't both run at the same spot"...

2. If you ever DC or have connection issues, there is no return. You get kicked out and your team is fighting a 2vs3. The game is literally impossible to win then and you cannot return. More than that - there is no connection indicator, so it's hard to tell if your ally is lagging (and therefor cannot defend) or they are just terrible. The game is so fast-paced that if you lag even a slight bit, it's unplayable.

3. Really poor UI. It's very difficult to tell where anything is hidden - and the menus in combat rapid-fire information at you. Also the buffs/items you are offered to choose in competitive matches pass so fast that it's hard to consider what you want to build (and they are chosen at random and an opponent can get one before you - locking you out of that choice) - which makes picking your build extremely difficult unless you memorize every single item form a big pile...

4. The game outcome is EXTREMELY determined by your team. If your Goalie knows to "stay and Defend - pass the ball to whoever is not swarmed" and your Fronts just "pass the ball between each other - don't swarm the same spot" -> you will absolutely COOK the enemy team. But the very moment you are the only one who knows this simple, common football tactic -> you automatically lose. There is no carry potential here at all solo.

Overall - this is a VERY fun game. But wow, your teammates can utterly destroy your game. It's worse than League of Legends in how utterly screwed you get by bad teams. The matches go by fast, but I literally cannot recommend it unless you enjoy yelling at the screen. 

Also - side note to the developers if they are reading this.
There is literally NOTHING INTERESTING in your cash shop. I checked it out and no item on the Season Pass makes me even lightly interested in a purchase. Your characters have like ONE SKIN each, some of them looking super-similar to the base one, maybe with the exception of Juno. And some characters have NOTHING there. 
Even when I was looking for something to buy - there was NOTHING to buy...

Yet in Keywords, there's no definition for Strikes. Whether its a K.O or a Goal which are obvious definitions, strikes sounds like a baseball or even soccer/football term. 
Another example: Pummelers: "Gain 15% Speed whenever you have a Striker advantage". What IS an "Advantage"? Even if its pointed out in the tutorial (I'm a beta tester, did this years ago so i don't remember) it should be reminded what these are or rephrased to be more obvious or linked to a term from the Keywords.

Design 6/10: Characters excel at one thing but some are better than others when their traits overlap but they all can essentially score a goal- however, i cannot comprehend why X is a bigger brawler than every other character, making him a meta pick in every rank and a perma ban. Or characters like Luna who are really good at Goalie but given 1 item (Eject Button) makes them a 2v3 situation and excel at range vs every other ranged character- specially forward-focused like Estelle or Kai. It is simply unfair and asymmetrical.

If two characters overlap on traits and their kit is focused towards Goalie, do NOT give them perks to cover other roles because it makes 2v3 situation. "Goalie diff" they say.

Competitive scene 7/10: The game keeps me at the edge of my seat and it's fun, the vibe and emotion is there. However, 1 ban isn't enough because 1 pick can ruin the game- and if they MVP, they get first dibs on item- therefore making them even a bigger MVP. This makes comebacks and catching up impossible as some characters only require 1 or 2 items to fully stomp a team (like Vyce, Rasmus, Luna and Rune).
There should be a 2nd ban after each team picks 1 character.

Content 4/10: As much as i love the simplicity of Daily/Weekly/Seasonal/Event (Events should have a different colors to Seasonal missions, maybe green?). Such events like "Play 10 games with friends" isn't an event. Its a day-to-day basis if you have people to play with. Even if it encourages to play with friends- what about the solo players?. 

"Get ready to get pre-made stomped by 3 people because we don't have matchmaking based on premades". That's how the event currently feels- specially when they're all experienced players and you can see that.

AFK/Leavers/Friendly-fire 10/10: You WILL find these at least 8 out of 10 times unless you go premade. And when they add skill-based matchmaking- it could get better or worse. I hope the devs add a system that checkmarks players based on their actions in a match, whether they stand at the goalie doing nothing or (if they're the a goalie) spending time in the wrong part of the map and not doing their job. You could also make conditions that they need to make based on their role in order to avoid these checkmarks so they don't get suspended.
And after 3 checkmarks, you can either suspend them to not get rewards with X amount of redemption games so they can get their rewards back.
Or after 5 checkmarks with redemption games left, straight-up ban them for X days or until next season. Also each report to X player add checkmarks towards suspension or ban. I am SICK of going Queue > Play > End > Report on EVERY game because of these people.

Can't wait for next season (or the current one) for smurfs where  you'll see high ranking players stomp low ranks- which should be another reason for reports since it ruins the competitiveness and player experience in all contexts.

Omega Strikers, aka "Anime Air Hockey," has the potential to be the best competitive multiplayer game since the launch of Valorant.

+ Simple to understand, yet complex and difficult to master
+ Little to no toxicity as the ONLY form of communication between you and others is via emotes / gestures
+ Playing as a coordinated 3-stack will consistently beat out rando solo queue teams
+ Matches are fast-paced -- each individual set is only a few minutes long, and even a full 5-game match is over in 20 minutes tops, while most are done in 10-12 minutes
+ Ability draft between rounds is an incredible concept that rewards strong performance, allows for builds and synergies, and can still give a team that is behind a fighting chance
+ Removing the boring and overly wrought Trainings system in favor of the abilities and draft is a GENIUS change!
+ Engaging characters that have their own unique aesthetics, playstyles, deep lore, rewards for playing as them, and character themes that are dope as hell and will play mid-match if your character tops the scoreboard at the end of the round
+ Very fair free-to-play model that, as of this review, is not predatory or pay-to-win AT ALL
+ The developer, Odyssey, is VERY active with the community (and have been since the first closed alpha test) and listens to feedback
+ A variety of fields that are all unique and, for the most part, fun to play, and it really allows for variety during long play sessions
+ Smart marketing with outreach to creators and contacting esports organizations to coordinate events
+ A huge degree of polish for the developer's first title, and it has come a LOOOONG way since the first alpha tests
+ An absolute banger of a soundtrack that will expand with every new character added to the game
+ The opening cinematic by Studio Trigger!! My God, is it good!
+ Lots of great customization with emotes, nameplates, titles, skins, and more!

Now, to be fair, the game does have a few down sides:
- Currently not very many options to let players practice and learn outside of regular matches. As of writing this there IS a co-op VS AI mode which helps and Odyssey has stated they're working on a true Training mode, so this will improve!
- Playing on a controller feels clunky at-best and a bit awkward, including menu navigation
- Too many things are buried behind layers of menus in unintuitive places
- Current battle pass is listed as 120 days, or 4 months -- that MAY be too long, time will tell
- Changing your profile is awful right now -- the menu is poorly constructed and needs an overhaul
- A stage ban phase or comp map pool (similar to games like Siege) would be nice to have once the game has more maps to choose from
- The newest characters feel a bit overpriced for both free credits and-real money -- in my opinion characters should ONLY be purchasable via free currency or some kind of premium pass akin to Smite or the different editions of Siege that give you new characters in perpetuity or in a bundle
- A few glitches, albeit nothing game breaking, at the moment (devs are aware and working on it)
- No great solutions or punishments for AFK / leavers as of now, even in Ranked

I'd love to recommend this because the core of the game is solid but there are a few crippling problems. Things may improve so check other reviews if this one isn't updated.

[b]The main one is crossplay with mobile devices. It needs a toggle.[/b] It's impossible to enjoy the game when these people afk to wipe their butt in the middle of the match or can't find the button to hit the puck) to save their life. I don't want to dunk on people but jesus christ, it has to be said, I have never seen a more idiotic playerbase. A colony of amoebas would be smarter. The mobile crowd just cannot focus which is a disaster for a team-based game. You will absolutely hate your teammates. On top of that mobile is inherently unstable which leads to a large amount of matches with quitters, sometimes on both teams. If you decide to play this game, please bring a friend with you. Solo queuing is a surefire way to trigger an aneurysm.

[b]Another problem is the draft system in normal and competitive matches[/b]. After each set (there are up to 5 sets in a match), you get to pick an "awakening." Only one person can pick each item, and the order is determined by how well each player did. [b]It's a rich get richer system that starts very early and can determine the outcome of the entire match after the very first set.[/b] When I am the first person to pick it leads me to be completely overpowered compared to everyone else, even my teammates. When I don't pick first, I am gimped for the rest of the match and have to fight an increasingly uphill battle on top of the score gap. This also means that you are competing against your own teammates for important, build-defining items. I have heard that it used to be a loadout system in the beta and people seem to like that system more than this new one. I've unfortunately not played the beta, but what I'm sure of is that I hate this system. The snowballing is too strong. When the match is set after the first round, what point is there to play the other rounds?

This leads me to my next point, [b]randomness[/b], which I will call rng from now on. What items are available to draft in competitive are completely random, which means the enemy could get access to gamebreaking items for their characters while you stand blue-balled as nothing appears for you. You can choose to grab their items (assuming you are above on the pick order) but denying the enemy doesn't feel nearly as good as making yourself stronger. I honestly believe this kind of rng should have no part in a competitive setting.
RNG is unfortunately also present in other game modes. You cannot escape it. In quickplay you are given a set of items that may or may not have a theme. This pressures everyone to pick characters that work with these items rather than characters that you would like to play and enjoy. For example if the theme is "creation" (buffing the strength, duration and size of constructs) then the incentive to play Juno, Dubu or Rune is high as these characters will be massively boosted.
[b]When I play a video game, one with choices such as a roster of character, I go in with a plan. "Today I would like to play Estelle" for example. I don't want the game to make decisions for me.[/b]
Again, it seems the game was completely different in beta and you could choose what items to bring in at the start, allowing you to play who YOU want to play. I'm greatly disappointed that this is the way they chose to go.

Bugs. There are still a lot of things that don't work or aren't consistent.
Off the top of my head, the bursting mechanic which lets you prime the puck, preventing anyone but yourself from hitting it with a super powered strike, sometimes actually lets anyone hit it, using all the meter saved up (which takes a while to fill). It's incredibly frustrating.
The server it picks for North America seems to be inconsistent. Sometimes you will have good ping, sometimes you'll reach 200ms because I think it picked a server on the furthest coast.
Some numbers like Affinity (points and levels you get linked to a certain character to unlock some of their cosmetics) don't update until you restart the game.

Twitch culture. This one is going to be subjective and perhaps sound a bit petty to some, but let me attempt to explain. The game has beautifully drawn cosmetics and emotes in the style of the rest of the game. They are cute, sometimes even funny, and they fit right into the game. Some even reference cultural things, and I'm not against that. The important thing is that they perfectly fit the tone and style of this cartoon/anime game. On the other hand, there are twitch emotes that are straight up faces of various streamers I assume were sponsored to play this game. They are ugly and completely out of style. You may enjoy seeing moist critical's photo mid match but I really don't, and it happens quite a lot. If they were at least drawn to be in line with the rest of emotes I'd have a lesser reaction to them. As they are, I am waiting for a mod or toggle to hide them because they really do throw me out of the experience.

All in all it seems to be a decent game encumbered by a few bad decisions. The good thing is that it's not completely irreversible, but some of choices will be hard to make for the developers. Allowing people to opt into crossplay might make queues slightly longer, but I guarantee that all pc players will be grateful to be able to choose whether or not their teammates have the IQ of a rock.

I waited a long time for Omega Strikers to come back from the public beta and it was disappointing how it turned out. The decisions made between the beta and release just do not make any sense. 

Awakenings: This is what replaced the Trainings from the beta and instead of being able to pick out a skill tree you are RNGed into your Awakenings. What adds insult to injury is you can also get the Awakening you want STOLEN which often forces you to pick an Awakening which is either not great on your character or one you cannot even benefit from at all. The idea of additional perks as rounds go on is interesting on paper, if there was one system that worked like the old Trainings and the Awakenings were their own thing that could somewhat remedy this problem. You only get one Awakening in Quick-Play which makes the gameplay feel more sluggish. 

Rounds: This game is primarily advertised as fast-paced and quick. The rounds system is counter-intuitive to this by dragging out games to be at least twice as long as they would have been if the default format for competitive was still what is now Quick-Play Mode. Makes for an interesting game mode, but it messes up pacing in the game. When normal or competitive matches ran long it was mentally exhausting. 

Goal Paddles: These also mess up pacing quite a bit as the majority of a round is not devoted to scoring but to breaking down these barriers. Especially in maps with 2 of these Paddles, if all maps only had one this would not be too much of a problem.  

I would chalk up my problems with the release of Omega Strikers to the poor pacing of the new "normal mode" and mechanics that while interesting on paper make the game much less  enjoyable due to either the RNG of it or how it messes with pacing. I'm ultimately indifferent about the Gear mechanic. It is sad to see a game with this much potential to mess up this badly.

Omega Strikers is a unique game that boasts great character designs, fast-paced gameplay, and a lack of chat that prevents toxic players from spreading negativity. The game allows players to take on the role of a goalie or forward, contributing both defensively and offensively to the team's success. The game's design pushes boundaries, which is impressive in a climate where many developers are afraid to be seen as insensitive or objectifying.

However, despite its merits, the game's marketing needs improvement. Despite the trailer receiving over 2 million views, the game does not seem to be well-known, and there are no popular videos with tens of thousands of views. Many people have trouble understanding what the game actually is, and it is difficult to explain unless you have played it. The game also has issues with players AFKing during a match, which ruins the experience for everyone involved.

To address this issue, stiffer penalties or automatic replacement by AI could be implemented. Another problem with the game is that players are unable to lock in their preferred striker upon pressing "Play." This means that there are occasions when two players want to play the same character, leading to frustration.

The official Omega Strikers Discord community is also a source of annoyance. Although it is meant to be a place for discussion and support, it is filled with weirdos who are only interested in sexual fan fiction of the characters, even in the main or general channels. Players who are not interested in this content are advised to avoid the official Discord community.

Despite these issues, Omega Strikers is still worth trying, as it is free and very different from other games. Its unique gameplay and character designs make it a refreshing change from the more traditional offerings on the market. However, it would benefit from better marketing and more player-friendly features, such as the ability to lock in preferred characters and stricter penalties for AFKing.

One of those rare cases where a game gets the free-to-play model right. I really hope this works out for the devs cause this is something pretty unique and I feel like it could go pretty far. Characters are distinct and charming, the playstyles are varied, there's some surprisingly cool arena designs that genuinely shake things up, and the core gameplay is solid. Not perfect, but solid. And for a free game it's hard to complain too much, but the devs clearly want this to be something really competitive. Other people have done far better analyzing the mechanics than I could though, so I'll just stick to the stuff I like.

Characters can only be unlocked by playing and completing daily/weekly/seasonal objectives. You can't just buy all the characters with real money. All the purchasable stuff instead goes to cosmetics. But you can still unlock some pretty fun stuff just by specializing in certain characters, and progressing through the usual multiplayer game thing of "you got enough arbitrary xp so here's a neat new cosmetic thing." Basically, I don't really feel like I'm missing out on anything that's significantly cooler than what I could just unlock for free. The coolest stuff to me is the characters anyway, so I'm plenty satisfied.

There's also no voice or text chat, and I feel it's definitely for the better. Instead you have some quick call-outs and cute emoticons you can use super quickly and easily. Which in a frantic, fast-paced game like this, works much better imo. Also, since it's a competitive game without those usual chat features, you don't have to worry about any awkward situations where someone makes a fool of themselves because they got too invested. It's hard to tell without those features, but the community does generally seem very welcoming. People were always spamming heart emotes after a goal and stuff, it was cute lol.

In the open beta, Omega Strikers was a great game. It is no longer any good. Here are the changes:
   
    - The score limit used to be first to 5 points, and you had to win by at least 2 points. Now it is a best of 5 series of first-to-3-point sets. This, along with other changes, makes the game take much longer (approx 20 mins), and now feels more like a chore. It is also much less exciting because the impact of a single goal is now minimal due to there being up to 5 sets.
  
  - The special/ultimate ability is not allowed until level 2. Why would they think this was a good idea?

    - The characters used to have 'trainings' which were used to make loadouts for the heroes, each one giving modifiers so you could make a loadout in order to play a certain style, and to make a loadout that played to the characters strengths. Now you only start a game with two modifiers (which are semi-random), and you collect one modifier between each bo3 set. You can't even guarantee that you will have a good loadout during the game, because you can't choose the same modifier that another player chose. In addition, this makes some characters completely useless and pathetic unless they can get specific modifiers (i.e. Kai with Perfect Form).

    - As a result of the trainings change, the first few sets have noticably more time spent simply sitting back waiting for cooldowns to reset. (I was wondering why the game felt so slow for a while, then I finally realized this is why).

    - Having all the extra time between sets picking up modifiers reduces time actually playing the game, making it less fun.

    - The default mapping for keybinds has changed, making it mildly annoying for players who played in the open beta. Even if these keys were better (they aren't), it just makes the player experience worse.

    - The goals have safeties on them every round. They need to be hit before the goal opens. The old system where it opened slowly, and would sometimes already be open completely at the start of the round was nicer, but now it feels like the game is trying to be as casual as possible. In addition, due to this it is now impossible to get a chaotic, exciting goal at the start of the round.

    - I significantly preferred the map variants during the beta, the new ones all seem to have a gimmick/weird feature, rather than just being a unique shape.

    - You can press q to temporarily become untargetable. If used well this would make it impossible for a bruiser character to KO(at least for the first few sets), because the abilities have very long cooldowns and loadouts no longer exist to reduce them.

All in all, it feels to me that the developers have tried to change the experience to cater to worse players. The goals have safeties so you have multiple chances to save, and if you lose a set, don't worry! You could get a modifier that the other team can't have that will make you stronger! All these anti-skill, anti-excitement changes make the game unfun, please revert them and bring the game back to its previous state that attracted so many people.

Finding a cool and unique game that is actually fun these days is rare, so seeing one kill itself right before my eyes is incredibly disappointing. 

The game in its beta state felt complete and was incredibly fun. Matches were fast paced and whichever team achieved five points, by a margin of two, won the match. Now, outside of quickplay, both teams have to reach three sets of three points with a pause in between sets for everyone to pick what were once trainings one could choose before a match. These are passive boosts to an aspect of a character that can help them reach their full potential, and are now erased after the match has ended. They are also random, which means you may not be able to play your character in your specific playstyle for what are now higher-stakes 20-30 minute matches. The magic of the previous version was how quickly you won if you were more skilled than your opponents, how quickly you lost if they were more skilled than you, and how tense matches got if both teams were equally skilled trying to get two points above the other. Losses didn't matter since you could easily get into another match afterwards, and getting on a win streak felt all the more satisfying. You could play hours of matches and not realise how much time has passed. Now matches are long enough to have one or two be exhausting. 

The developer's justification of the temporary, randomised trainings mid-match is that the longer the beta was live, the more similar each match felt. This was a good thing, as it allowed the players to become accustomed to their characters and how they were supposed to function given the right trainings for the player's playstyle. Now it is easy to forget which ones you chose in the 15 seconds your are given to chose when you consider how chaotic the actual gameplay is. Additionally, Counter-Strike hasn't changed in twenty years, and it seems to be doing well for itself. Having matches be similar is not a fault, but the current system 
they made to combat a non-issue is.

Another thing that makes matches take too long is the addition of what I will call goal-blocks. Previously, there were walls that retracted and extended throughout the match that blocked both goals. Whichever team was in the lead had their walls retract faster than the team losing, giving the team losing a chance to attack for a short time while their wall was still extended. Whoever is in the lead doesn't need an advantage over the other team, so the design at the time was good. Now there are goal-blocks. These are difficult to hit targets near each team's goals that will retract the walls once all are hit with the ball. This makes matches drag on, as one goalie can usually guard at least one of the goal-blocks for a long time, which means even more time spent in a game that used to have quick and fun matches. The charm of the worldwide beloved sport of football/soccer is that there's one person guarding a large goal with the help of the other players that are outside of the goal box, so adding a mechanic that makes it impossible to score unless you hit a prerequisite makes the game not fun.

Everything else that has changed is at most a minor annoyance, such as splitting up the end-game screen into three screens, so it's more difficult to share a screenshot of if you had a good game.

A common "gotcha" to the changes in ranked and the normal gamemodes include "Just play quickplay so you don't have to deal with the changes." What if you want to play the game you once loved with people around your skill level? Quickplay does not take skill level into account when forming players for a match, only ping. This means that the probability of completely destroying or being destroyed by the other team increases, and while it's nice for an ego boost, it's preferable to play opponents around your skill level to challenge yourself; Something you can no longer do if you prefer the previous version's gameplay compared the the current.

I will gladly change this review if these issues are fixed. It baffles me how a team can make a game for years, show off a fantastic pre-release product, and kill it in front of you when it was supposed to be finished.

Omega Strikers is a free, high-octane 3v3 tabletop hockey-brawler (I said what I said). It's also one of the only games where you can repeatedly punch a very ornery catgirl until they bounce around like a pinball and fly off the map. Need I say more?


[h1]The Short of It[/h1]
[i]See other sections for more detail, and the end for my concluding overall thoughts.[/i]

Alright, alright, I get it. Tabletop hockey-brawler might sound absurd. So I'll keep it brief: there's 1 yellow circle, 2 nets, and 6 players split into 2 groups of 3. Your goal? To score a goal. How? Simple! Get that yellow circle into the net, preferably the one that isn't yours, by "outwitting" the enemy goalie with the luckiest shot of your life—guaranteed to become the reason somebody uninstalls. Or, simply flip the core up into the air and smash that thing forwards at mach 10 directly into the opposing net.

If [i]patiently[/i] waiting for your forwards to finally score a goal sounds like fun, you can play as the goalie and become the enemy team's worst nightmare, laughing at their pitiful attempts to get past you all while earning the admiration of everyone after you kept the dream alive when all hope seemed lost. Well, tried to, anyway.


Omega Strikers thrives in its chaotic yet controlled gameplay, rewarding players for being at the center of that chaos. Did I mention there's no pay-to-win elements, a currency grind that isn't atrocious, a sizable amount of free-to-unlock cosmetics, and a battlepass where most items become purchasable in the shop after it ends? And this [i]isn't[/i] a sponsored review? [b][i]What?[/i][/b]


[h1]Story[/h1]
[i]If you would dare to call it that.[/i]

The setting here could be described as a Utopian society blessed with the most perfect and renewable energy source, enabling outstanding technology and magical abilities in a world where people really, REALLY love to play and watch their hyper-futuristic adaptation of hockey. If you like the idea of a gigantic hamster who grew ridiculously large after being fed copious amounts of tofu, or maybe a guy who's perfectly sane and only [i]maybe[/i] tries to inject highly condensed raw energy into people with the sole purpose of achieving superhuman abilities beyond what's already possible, you'll be right at home here.


[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
[i]This section is meant to be informative so that you can form your own opinion on if it sounds like it's something you'd enjoy.[/i]

[b]Omega Strikers can be punishing and shines particularly when playing with friends. Though the game is easy to pick up, there is absolutely a bit of a learning curve and you may find yourself lost in its highly reactive gameplay. However, if you're looking for something overflowing with sheer charm, or you like chasing the feeling of getting better at something, Omega Strikers checks both of those boxes.[/b]

Alright, onto the good part. The idea here is simple. Score goals for your team while stopping the enemy team from scoring goals of their own. Once you find yourself in the character selection screen and have picked one to play as, you'll choose an awakening, the game's name for powerful items capable of boosting your capabilities in various ways, alongside one of four gears specific to your role that provide similar benefits. During this screen you can also see the map—of which there are a few, each with their own gimmicks to spice up gameplay—that the match will play out in.

Loaded in? Here's what you need to know: the game plays out in sets. Score a goal by forcing the puck-shaped core into the enemy net after you've broken their goal barriers with that same core. First team to score three goals wins a set. First team to win three sets wins the game. A one minute timer, which resets after each goal, counts down to a sudden-death-esque overtime where the core starts to gradually speed up. On top of the 3 abilities unique to each character, everyone has two innate abilities known as Evade/Energy Burst and Strike, the former using a pool of energy to allow you to dodge abilities or send the core flying, and the latter acting as a way to redirect the core on a low cooldown.

After each set, everyone drafts one awakening from a list of 8, pulled randomly out of the current pool of 34. The order of picks is determined roughly by the experience individual players earned in the set leading up to the draft, plus some additional rules to help keep it fair. Experience is gained through things like knocking out enemy players by sending them off the map, striking the core, contesting the orbs that spawn, and of course scoring goals.

The game features ranked and unranked on top of a quickplay mode that serves as a faster, more casual alternative. You can play in custom 3v3s and they might occasionally throw in a for-fun gamemode like Rotating Goal Mode, where the maps get crazy and you forget how to tell up from down. Finally, there is an affinity/mastery system that allows you to level up each character as you play them, unlocking fun little cosmetics so you can show off that you don't know how to play anyone else because you've only touched one character for a length of time that you'd rather other people not discover.


[h1]Style & Design [/h1]
[i]Subjectivity warning![/i]

Omega Strikers is vibrant and playful. It leans into this in every aspect of its design. It has been described as "anime air hockey" numerous times and that's really not far off the mark. Some might love that, others not so much. Music follows the same philosophy and a lot of tracks are very energetic, generally well-suited for the style of game this is. Every character has their own theme that plays if they were the MVP in the previous set. The UI does its job and so there's not a whole lot to complain about, though it's not perfect and has subpar ultrawide support as of writing. In-game documentation is present and decently thorough; at the top-left of the main menu you can find a playbook that covers most terminology, game mechanics, and lists all the gears and awakenings.


[h1]Verdict [/h1]
[i]Or in the case of this review, my totally fair opinion.[/i]

If you've read all this, you ought to know by now that I highly recommend this game. While it no doubt has its fair share of flaws and issues, it is entirely free with a model that feels almost too reasonable, even including cross-progression and cross-platform play. And so, if you've read this far.. give it a try! You have nothing to lose. I sincerely hope this game gets the recognition it deserves, especially because I want the kind of practices it follows to be successful. Hence why I write this review at all.

I've had my eye on it for a while and the team that made it—from my perspective as a player—appears filled with enthusiasm for what they've created here, and are more than willing to listen to feedback. They come off as people who seem to genuinely want to put out a [i]game[/i], you know, those things that are meant to be fun and exciting, that everyone can enjoy. I'll mention here briefly that some players have mixed feelings on some of the changes made from the beta and that's fine. I largely enjoy them, but opinions and what have you. I'll say my piece, though; the team behind it recognized what the game lacked, and made changes in the hopes of improving it. From that, I'm confident they'll continue to do so given the chance. If you find yourself hopping in after reading this, and maybe notice some things you don't like so much or think could improve the game, tell them! They'll listen.

And finally, one last thing I want to mention is that the community is filled with truly great people who are more than willing to help out new players. So if you find the learning curve intimidating, don't hesitate to hop in the discord and ask a question or two, or maybe find some people to play with! I hope to catch you in the.. uh, footbrawl? Really? Look, just play the game. Thanks for reading.

The puck mechanics are also not well-thought-out as despite being a physics-based game, hits on it are always a pure 50/50 - either it goes one way or the other - which just leads to really tiring back-and-forth trades that honestly just feel like rock-paper-scissors, and heavily favour characters that can throw the most crap at once.

Matchmaking is also truly garbage, to the point where I struggle to believe that it's working properly. Ranked games in Omega Strikers are painfully long as they adopt a best out of 5 format, and it just feels like every single game is a complete mismatch with one team being clearly better than the other. What's worse is that the devs decided it would be a fantastic idea to launch a PvP team-based game in 2023 without any form of forfeit or surrender option, which would help get players out of lost games like this and save some mental. Oh yeah, and if anyone leaves or goes AFK mid-match then tough luck, you have to play out the entire rest of the game.

I wanted to like this game. I've been itching for a new PvP game to come out like this, and I did see some promise in it. However, the game has already grown stale for me and seems to be focused on casual enjoyment rather than competitive enjoyment, so unless they put good work in with future patches then I don't see me playing much more of Omega Strikers, if any.

Omega Strikers is best described as "3v3 air hockey with MOBA characters." Two teams of three take the field, each controlling a character with a set of unique abilities, and with them they must try to get a puck into the opposing team's goal. A relatively simple conceit is quickly made infinitely more complicated as you sling abilities (and the puck) all around the field to try to get a leg up over the competition. It's exhilarating, it's tense, it's hype as all hell.

Omega Striker's full release hasn't been without its complaints. Games now take place in a best-of-three format, with the first team to score three goals winning a set. Win three sets, win the game. In-between each set, both teams will draft "trainings" that give their characters new passive benefits. This system makes games take longer (15 minutes on average, I'd say), and introduces RNG; previously, you could select your awakenings as a build before the game began.

However, I actually like this system a lot! Frankly, the only training system had very little build diversity. Most people were just gonna slap on the most meta trainings and get on with it. I think making it so you can't always get the best trainings for your character introduces some fun variance, and forces you to think about what you can make the most use out of when you can't always be optimal. Sure, Juno WANTS things that makes her creations better, but I like thinking about what else I can make use of when there are no creation trainings (or they're all taken).

Omega Strikers is a ton of fun, and I think the devs are on the right track with their changes in the full release. I really hope and pray for its continued success; nothing would depress me more than seeing an announcement in six months that they have to take the servers offline. Omega Strikers oozes style and provides infinite opportunity for hype plays, so I think anybody with the stomach for competitive games should definitely give it a shot.

+The entire concept is amazing. It takes the simple idea of airhockey or soccer and turns it a mini-moba. The only 2 roles are Goalie and Forward. Both have access to different items but many characters can be both. While you want to hit the puck, you also can attack the enemy and try to push them into the walls of the arena, KOing them Super Smash Bros style and putting them on a cooldown.

+The characters are really varied and feel unique. One character has the ability to shoot out shield walls and barriers and heal and rez the team. One character has the ability to throw down slime blobs which act as mini-summons and can use them to ricochet the puck at crazy angles. One character can straight up punch and attack other characters and bully them. 

+The stages feel unique. One stage has a barrier in the middle that blocks shots while also having a speed boost in the middle. One stage has a black hole in the middle that will suck the puck and characters into the center. It can be used to curve the puck around things or detonated to injure the enemy team. Theres a stage where the upper and lower parts of the arena have convayer belts that allow you to zip across the arena. 

+Extremely quick games. This isn't like League or Dota where you will get stuck in a 30-45 minute losing game you can't quit. Most games are over by 10 minutes. The matches are extremely fast paced and intense and require you to focus. Even after going on a losing streak in a match, you can get some good items that can completely turn the table.

+Non-predatory micro transactions and some neat extras. Normally I don't care about banners or emoticons or skins but some of the ones available for you to unlock for free, and paid look awesome and often are goofy and parody internet culture.

+Great controller support. I've been playing on controller the entire time and after you get used to the controls it feels like a twin-stick shooter. Its rare I've launched the puck the wrong direction due to bad controls.

Cons:

-The UI for the menus aren't great. All of the unlocks are not sorted so you have to scroll through everything to see what you got. 

-There is no filter or great explanation for any of the characters on if they would be better for certain roles. The move sets descriptions have no videos to show you what exactly the moves do, and with no practice mode that I could find, you basically have to youtube videos to see what the characters do and how they should be played.

-This is not really a con, but this is not a game you can kind of sit back and relax and play. The matches are extremely intense and every role needs to have constant awareness of the entire arena at all times.
